Address: Chinatown Complex Market & Food Centre, #02-168, 335 Smith Street, 050335, Singapore
Description: Two shops share the same venue, so be sure you order from the right one. The grilled-to-order satay comes in pork, chicken and lamb varieties (or an assortment). The nutty, tangy sauce is tasty and you can order rice on top.

Address: Tekka Centre, #01-326, 665 Buffalo Road, 210665, Singapore
Description: The stall dates back to 1920s. Dry noodles dressed in sambal sauce are topped with bean sprouts, prawns and pork, and served with umami-laden prawn soup. Or opt for the noodle soup version. Add fried shallots and lard on top.

Address: Golden Mile Food Centre, #01-91, 505 Beach Road, 199583, Singapore
Description: Their fried kway teow boasts exceptional wok hei and is pork free. Topped with leafy greens, cockles, egg, bean sprouts, deep-fried anchovies and a prawn, the noodles are perfectly seasoned. It closes when sold out.

Address: Amoy Street Food Centre, #01-39, 7 Maxwell Road, 069111, Singapore
Description: The stall has an interesting look and sells local, traditional noodles cooked in an innovative way.

Restaurant Name: Adam Rd Noo Cheng Big Prawn Noodle
Address: Adam Food Centre, #01-27, 2 Adam Road, 289876, Singapore
Description: The prawn mee cooked à la minute is a recipe from the owner’s father. Opt for “dry” noodles tossed in prawn paste of your desired level of heat, alongside a bowl of prawn soup. Toppings like pig skin add contrasting textures.

Address: Hong Lim Market and Food Centre, #02-64, Blk 531A, Upper Cross Street, 051531, Singapore
Description: The taste of duck meat blends with the spice marinade, each boasting a rich flavour. Snacks like duck liver and dried tofu are also offered.

Address: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, #01-27, 20 Kensington Park Road, 557269, Singapore
Description: Serves fried Hokkien noodles with shrimp and squid.

Restaurant Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Address: Amoy Street Food Centre, #01-14, 7 Maxwell Road, 069111, Singapore
Description: Now run by the third generation, this family-run stall is famous for its fish ball noodle soup topped with ground pork, pork liver, seaweed and pork rinds. Pork ribs are simmered for hours resulting in a broth rich in gutsy flavours.

Address: Tekka Centre, #01-229/232, 665 Buffalo Road, 210665, Singapore
Description: The family has been selling its famous biryani since the 1950s. The set comes with yellow basmati rice enhanced by a spice mix; mutton, chicken or fish curry; and papadums. The mutton sambal is tender and tasty.

Address: Newton Food Centre, #01-27, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, 229495, Singapore
Description: Come here for cooked-to-order seafood at a range of prices. Barbecue is hugely popular, but you can also opt for sambal, black pepper sauce or salted egg yolk. Don’t miss the cereal butter prawns.

Address: #04-48, One Raffles Place, 048616, Singapore
Description: In case you're curious about the name (or perhaps you guessed), this place serves a 6- to 10-course omakase-style tasting menu, showcasing diverse flavours from across India. Chef Robin champions a refined take on Indian cuisine, using solid French techniques and ingredients from West Bengal, Gujarat and Sri Lanka. Elegant smaller dishes are meticulously prepared for a balance of flavours. Perfectly paired with their Indian-inspired cocktails.

Address: #01-08, 1 Shenton Way, 068803, Singapore
Description: If there is one dish that customers expect to find in a restaurant called Anglo Indian, it is chicken tikka masala, and, sure enough, it is a bestseller in this simply decorated eatery in the heart of the CBD. The dining room may only seat 20, but there is a large outdoor terrace that is often packed. Other popular choices from the sensibly priced menu include butter chicken and mutton dum biryani. The weekday lunch is a steal.

Address: Chinatown Complex Market & Food Centre, #02-112, 335 Smith Street, 050335, Singapore
Description: Popiah filled with ingredients such as eggs, shrimp, carrot, peanuts, etc. affords rich, varied flavours. The deep-fried spring rolls are crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside and loaded with big-boned oomph.

Address: ABC Brickworks Market & Food Centre, #01-141, Blk 6 Jalan Bukit Merah, 150006, Singapore
Description: Eight kinds of MSG-free slow-boiled soups, including the signature ginseng Silkie chicken soup that boasts a mild herbal taste are on the menu here. All are served with pumpkin rice or steamed rice. Come early to beat the crowds.

Address: Mondrian Duxton, #01-08, 83 Neil Road, 089813, Singapore
Description: Chilean chefs Araya and Guerrero worked at the same restaurant in China. Their ingenious creations – deeply influenced by Araya's time in Spain and Japan – use an eclectic mix of Chilean and Japanese produce, with a South Pacific theme. Japanese favourites such as kinki and cod milt are jazzed up by aji amarillo and merkén from Chile, served alongside French pigeon and caviar. They even ferment and roast their own cacao to use in sauces.

Address: 51 Old Airport Road Food Centre, #01-110, 51 Old Airport Road, 390051, Singapore
Description: Fluffy and spongy pancakes are made to order with a wheat flour batter and no eggs. Vegan fillings include shredded coconut, red bean paste, and peanuts. Lacto vegetarians may go for cheese or chocolate filling.

Address: Adam Food Centre, #01-10, 2 Adam Road, 289876, Singapore
Description: Since 1973, this stall has been serving its secret mutton soup recipe. The broth is rich, dense, and full of herbal flavours. Apart from the popular leg, also try other lamb cuts. Order bread to mop up the broth.

Address: 165 Tanjong Pagar Road, 088539, Singapore
Description: The Alsace-born chef takes diners on a culinary journey to his homeland with authentic regional specialties such as choucroute garnie and tarte flambée aux escargots. International dishes are also popular, like Malaysian rotisserie free-range chicken and a selection of beefsteaks dry aged in-house and chargrilled to perfection. Service is attentive and helpful. Start or end the night with a drink on the terrace or at the bar.

Restaurant Name: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Address: Whampoa Makan Place, #01-46, 90/91 Whampoa Drive 91, 320091, Singapore
Description: The sliced fish bee hoon (rice vermicelli) comes in a flavourful, milky fish stock, with fried garlic bits for extra fragrance and crunch. Also worth trying are the tom yam soup, seafood soup and fried fish head bee hoon.

Address: Bedok Interchange Hawker Centre, #01-19, 208 New Upper Changi Road, 460208, Singapore
Description: The freshly steamed chwee kueh rice cakes are soft and velvety and the sauce on top made with preserved radish, scallion, dried shrimps and chilli is simply irresistible. May be closed without prior notice.

Address: Level 2, 269A Beach Road, 199546, Singapore
Description: Belimbing refers to "starfruit", a versatile ingredient in Asian cooking. The bustling open kitchen is set against sage green walls and wood trims that impart serenity. The menu features traditional Singaporean fare with creative twists. Corn salat is a nod to kueh salat, reimagined with sweet corn and brown butter for nutty, toasty sweetness. Paired with assam pedas and white pepper sauce, the silky clam custard boasts layers of flavour.

Address: #01-05, 1 Claymore Drive, 229594, Singapore
Description: Solid wood furniture, rattan pendant lamps and wagon wheel chandeliers impart modern boho chic in this bright, cosy space with two levels. The chef recounts his memories and personal story through a menu that encompasses meat dishes, as well as vegetarian, gluten-free and vegan options. Inspired by Indian street food, the signature Indori beetroot tikki is big on flavours with a hint of sweetness from the corn.

Address: #01-05, 63 East Coast Road, 428776, Singapore
Description: A mesmerising array of top-quality gelato and sorbet is served in house-made thyme-scented waffle cones. Sea salt hojicha, white chrysanthemum, and raspberry lychee are some of its outstanding offerings.

Address: 50 Dunlop Street, 209379, Singapore
Description: Biryani is the standout dish in this place specialising in North Indian food. The lamb shank biryani is recommended for its fork-tender texture and meaty flavour. Haleem, mutton nihari and aloo gobi are also good choices.

Address: 25 Keong Saik Road, 089132, Singapore
Description: This relaxing, inviting bistro serves classic French fare that impresses with its mindful preparation, solid skills and exceptional quality. A Burgundian himself, the friendly owner fashions a menu that captures the best-known recipes of his home region, including oeuf en meurette, beef bourguignon and pôchouse, alongside classic sweets such as profiteroles and Paris-Brest. The well-curated wine list covers a wide selection of Burgundian labels.

Address: 399, 401, 403 Balestier Road, 329801, Singapore
Description: You won’t have any trouble finding this enduringly popular restaurant – its colourful neon sign will guide you in from afar. The group may have expanded over the years but this is the original branch, opened in 1983. Their signature boiled chicken, which boosts succulent and tender meat, is still the biggest draw and comes in three different sizes, but those looking for a full zi char feast won’t be disappointed. Avoid peak times if you’re not prepared to queue.

Address: Zion Riverside Food Centre, #024, 70 Zion Road, 247792, Singapore
Description: Boon Tong Kee prides itself on its spiced soy marinade made with aromatic Chinese herbs. With its springy skin and tasty meat, the signature braised duck is a hit. The braised pork trotter and taro rice are also popular.

Address: Victoria Concert Hall, #01-01, 11 Empress Place, 179558, Singapore
Description: An outpost of its namesake in Stockholm, this is the brainchild of the Swedish owner-chef Björn Frantzén. Nestled in the historical Victoria Concert Hall (1800s), its retro glamour complements the chef's new spin on brasserie classics, some with trolley or tableside service. Try the råraka, a Swedish potato cake topped with vendace roe, crème fraîche, chives and red onion. Toast Astoria with prawn, king crab and wasabi aioli is also unmissable.

Address: 126 Tanjong Pagar Road, 088534, Singapore
Description: Diners flock to this small neighbourhood joint and it’s easy to understand why: the bubbly, charming hostess works seamlessly with her husband chef from Veneto, who in turn delivers simple, delicious Italian fare with subtle Asian twists. Try his tau kwa tower – an appetising mix of sautéed Italian-style greens and Singaporean dried tofu salad in a tangy Asian dressing. Hand-made pasta is another highlight, as are the weekly specials.

Address: 29 Scotts Road, 228224, Singapore
Description: The entrance to this intimate restaurant in a refurbished colonial house is flanked by an imposing display of wine bottles, including many interesting Italian vintages. The interior is elegantly furnished with refined contemporary charm. They serve set menus comprising impeccably executed dishes. Signatures include house-made tagliatelle with freshly shaved and intensely aromatic white truffle. Wine list comes with options of Italian labels, natural wine and whisky flyer.

Address: #01-04, 7 Dempsey Road, 249671, Singapore
Description: Years ago, the Aussie owner-chef David Pynt opened a pop-up in London called Burnt Enz to great acclaim. Then his refined barbecue food cooked in a wood-fire brick kiln was taken up a notch with Burnt Ends in Singapore. In 2021, it moved to this location, twice as big as its previous space. The small but interesting snack menu is worth exploring. Meats and fish are well complemented by the Australian wines on offer. Book ahead to secure a table.

Address: Raffles Arcade, #02-02, 328 North Bridge Road, 188719, Singapore
Description: Wood-fire cooking is the speciality of this dark and handsome restaurant within Raffles hotel. Head straight to the tasting menu if you want to experience a variety of top-quality fish and meat dishes, all expertly prepared using American wood and supplemented with Asian flavours. The moodily lit room ensures your gaze never wanders too far from the open kitchen. A restaurant to appeal to the hunter-gatherer in all of us.

Address: The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands, Galleria Level, #B1-71, 10 Bayfront Avenue, 018972, Singapore
Description: Synonymous with quality steaks with big flavours, celebrity chef Wolfgang Puck is a seal of confidence for this outpost of his famed namesake in LA. Here steaks are expertly seasoned, chargrilled and finished off under a 1200-degree broiler to leave them juicy and tender. Don’t forget to order the amazing onion rings with your steak. The wine list offers over 650 labels and a cocktail at the bar while waiting for your table adds to the experience.

Address: 17A Dempsey Road, 249676, Singapore
Description: The lofty room feels airy, while bamboo and rattan details impart serenity. Influenced by his mother and grandma, the chef cooks traditional Peranakan fare with a creative twist and an Indonesian touch. In addition to à la carte dishes that are served communal style, the tasting menu features 10+ courses that change every two months; many are one-bite dishes with unique flavours and textures.

Address: #01-03, 5B Portsdown Road, 139311, Singapore
Description: Ce Soir wins kudos not only for its impossibly romantic floral theme and all things botanical, but also for its deftly crafted French fare with distinct Asian notes. Inspired by the chef's childhood memories, a recent iteration of the menu prominently featuring Japanese produce is presented as a scrapbook. Each and every course of the lunch set and dinner tasting menus is visually stunning, with seafood being a definite highlight.

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Address: 115 Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre, #01-51, Blk 115 Bukit Merah View, 151115, Singapore
Description: The mutton soup here can be paired with tripe, meatballs, tendon or even brain. The mutton boasts the right mix of fatty and lean meat, without tasting gamey. The broth has a mildly herbal flavour. Come early as they tend to sell out.

Address: Blk C, #01-34, Jackson Square, 11 Lorong 3 Toa Payoh, 319579, Singapore
Description: This joint specialises in noodle soup with wontons and char siu – the springy noodles are shipped from Hong Kong; the lightly charred pork has layers of fat and lean meat. For extra texture and flavour, order shredded abalone on top.

Restaurant Name: Cheng Heng Kway Chap and Braised Duck Rice
Address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-05, 44 Holland Drive, 270044, Singapore
Description: The name reveals the two signature dishes – the braised duck is tender, has robust flavours and is accompanied by a perfectly seasoned, spiced soy marinade. The kway (rice noodles) are silky smooth and the soup is moreish.

Address: Geylang Bahru Market & Food Centre, #01-35, 69 Geylang Bahru, 330069, Singapore
Description: Its famous soy-marinated duck boasts velvety flesh on a bed of steamed rice perfumed by duck scents. It comes with chilli vinegar that aptly cuts through the richness, plus an aromatic duck soup made with Chinese herbs.

Address: 127 Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-30, Blk 127, Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, 310127, Singapore
Description: The pan-fried radish cake is hugely popular. Fried on one side until golden, it allows you to taste the caramelised crispy bits and the soft moist cake at the same time. The cakes are fried to order, so expect a longer waiting time.

Address: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, #01-34, 20 Kensington Park Road, 557269, Singapore
Description: Opt for pork, chicken, mutton or ketupat served with pineapple sauce.

Address: 20 Ghim Moh Road Market & Food Centre, #01-04, Blk 20, Ghim Moh Road, 270020, Singapore
Description: Juicy and flavoursome braised duck is served with rice, congee, kway teow or noodles, plus optional extras such as duck gizzard, duck liver or marinated egg. The "set" comes with a bowl of bak kut teh.

Address: Golden Mile Food Centre, #01-59, 505 Beach Road, 199583, Singapore
Description: Three options feature on the menu of this stall – chilli mee, prawn mee and laksa. Go for chilli mee: yellow egg noodles topped with tangy chilli sauce, pork ribs, prawns, hard-boiled egg, fish cake and tofu puffs.

Address: 39C Harding Road, 249541, Singapore
Description: From chef Julien Royer of Odette fame comes this classic French brasserie, named after his mother. It's housed in a lovely converted 1930s chapel with an open kitchen at one end and a bar at the other. Those with a fondness for comforting French classics will find the roll call of favourites highly appealing, from foie gras terrine to vol-au-vents and soufflé. The wine list is thoughtfully curated and by-the-glass choices abound.

Address: 84 Amoy Street, 069903, Singapore
Description: In addition to naming his venture after the Tim Winton book, Sri Lankan chef Rishi Naleendra pays homage to Australia where he honed his skills. His food embodies balance and harmony, making the best use of top-quality ingredients and well thought-out flavours. Highlights include Sri Lankan curry with blue marron and coconut broth, and Murray cod with fermented bell pepper and almonds. The savvy front-of-house team delivers slick service and the perfect vibe.

Restaurant Name: Come Daily Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee
Address: 127 Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-27, Blk 127, Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, 310127, Singapore
Description: The signature Hokkien prawn mee is made with yellow egg noodles, rice vermicelli and squid, topped with fried crispy lard that adds an extra layer of texture and flavours.

Address: 50 Tras Street, 078989, Singapore
Description: This friendly restaurant serves authentic Indonesian fare in a setting adorned with artefacts and bamboo-styled furnishings. The signature whole grilled squid Cumi Bali – succulent and springy in texture – is the restaurant’s namesake and is even more delicious in their renowned house-made sauce that features a myriad of natural spices. Nasi Kunyit is a rice dish jazzed up with 11 spices, including turmeric, cinnamon and pandan leaves. The portion sizes are perfect for sharing.

Address: Golden Mile Food Centre, #B1-53, 505 Beach Road, 199583, Singapore
Description: This stall serves only curry chicken noodles and Hainanese chicken rice. The latter comes in three portion sizes. Choose between roast or steamed chicken. The steamed one boasts meaty flavour, springy skin and silky flesh.

Restaurant Name: Da Shi Jia Big Prawn Mee
Address: 89 Killiney Road, 239534, Singapore
Description: Guests are spoiled for choices here. First, pick between prawn noodle soup and fried prawn bee hoon. For prawn mee, specify the size of these wild-caught marine crustaceans – from regular to XXL. Then pick your noodles –the yellow variety, kway teow, bee hoon, or any combination of those. For real big eaters, choose extra toppings of fish cake, pork ribs or sliced pork. Don’t forget about snacks like tofu skin prawn rolls and fried prawn balls on the side.

Address: Tekka Centre, #01-266, 665 Buffalo Road, 210665, Singapore
Description: The experienced tandoor master knows his clay oven inside out. His fluffy, crispy naans have a loyal following. His grilled-to-order seekh kebab and chicken tikka masala are also exceptional and come in generous portions.

Address: 33 Duxton Road, 089497, Singapore
Description: Warm beige, wood tones and soft lighting make for a calm and soothing space. Similarly, dishes created by the Norwegian chef are simple and honest, with a touch of Nordic charm. At lunchtime, light meals such as toast, sandwiches and waffles are served. To experience his culinary vision in full, try his dinner set, which may include the unmissable "cod, kohlrabi, celeriac" – fresh, perfectly cooked fish finessed by solid technique.

Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-19, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
Description: This stall carries two varieties of tu tu kueh – coconut and peanut. The steamed rice cake is chewy and springy on the outside; both fillings are nutty, sweet and aromatic. Best enjoyed piping hot!

Address: Geylang Lorong 19, 323 Geylang Road, 389359, Singapore
Description: Frog is certainly big on the menu – besides the famous frog porridge, try frog fried with ginger and scallion or tossed in Kung Pao sauce. A favourite spot among locals for late-night supper, this place is always packed, so be prepared to wait.

Address: 16 Jiak Chuan Road, 089267, Singapore
Description: The main dining room of this shophouse just off Keong Saik Road is upstairs, but the best place to sit is at the ground-floor counter in front of the open kitchen, watching the chef and his team at work. The dishes are as flavoursome as they are colourful and creative. Order anchovy sticks with bottarga aioli while you peruse the menu’s sections: ‘snacks’, ‘soil’, ‘sea’ and ’land’. Octopus and suckling pig are the house signatures and the set menu is also worth trying.

Address: Chinatown Complex Market & Food Centre, #02-84, 335 Smith Street, 050335, Singapore
Description: Offers a wide array of noodles, including pork trotter and barbecue meats. The fresh yam noodles are handmade and available for take away only.

Address: Yuhua Village Market and Food Centre, #01-28, Blk 254, Jurong East Street 24, 600254, Singapore
Description: Popular stall for roasted meat and dumplings. Duck leg with shrimp wonton noodles is recommended. Come early before the food runs out.

Address: Taman Jurong Market & Food Centre, #03-146, 3 Yung Sheng Road, Jurong West, 618499, Singapore
Description: This popular stall offers lor mee with generous toppings like meatballs and fish flakes. The noodles are springy and the broth is tasty and flavoursome. Also, try their deep-fried prawn rolls with a crispy skin and juicy filling.

Address: Capella Hotel, 1 The Knolls, Sentosa Island, 098297, Singapore
Description: This restaurant in an ultra-luxury beach resort boasts a rustic chic room, complete with an open kitchen, wood-fired oven (hence the name) and a terrace overlooking the pool and garden. Here, the chef offers a good range of Italian classics, embodying his personal history and childhood memories. His tiramisu, generous enough for two to share, is topped with a crispy caramelised sugar shell, a perfect finale to the refined dining experience.

Address: 1300 East Coast Parkway, 468964, Singapore
Description: This white house styled after a masseria in Puglia is sited within East Coast Park. The sprawling lawn, spectacular ocean views and sound of the waves all exude a soothing vibe. The Pugliese chef is keen to bring authentic cuisine from his homeland to Singapore, of which focaccina and pasta made from scratch are the highlights. Try his San Marzano tomato focaccina with mozzarella and fresh basil, bursting with intense flavours.

Address: #01-01, 64 Tras Street, 079003, Singapore
Description: In this stylish eatery with a bar and an open kitchen, you’ll find the eponymous artisanal French salt on each table – but you won’t need it thanks to the owner-chef’s spot-on sense of seasoning. At this ‘bistro de luxe’ he delivers classical French cuisine with a light, modern spin – making it easy to save room for his signature Baba. Two set menus - we recommend the tasting menu for a global experience.

Address: 32 Keong Saik Road, 089139, Singapore
Description: You can’t miss the huge papier mâché caricatures of the owner and chef hanging from the ceiling. The food is equally fun as the chef melds Catalonian flavours with modern techniques to create original and exciting tapas-style dishes such as smoked Cantabrian anchovies on charcoal brioche, and patatas bravas FOC style. Always busy and buzzing with a cheerful vibe. Ask for a seat at the counter to enjoy the experience to the full.

Restaurant Name: Food Street Fried Kway Teow Mee
Address: Chinatown Complex Market & Food Centre, #02-173, 335 Smith Street, 050335, Singapore
Description: Loaded with wok hei, their kway teow mee is ribbon rice noodles, egg noodles, bean sprouts and scrambled egg tossed in a secret sauce. For toppings, choose clams only, or a mix of seafood with fish, squid, shrimps and clams.

Address: Berseh Food Centre, #02-40, 166 Jalan Besar, 208877, Singapore
Description: There is an array of Cantonese soups to choose from here. The eponymous soft-shelled turtle soup emits rich herbal aromas, served with plain steamed rice or taro rice.

Address: Redhill Market, #01-49, 85 Redhill Lane, 150085, Singapore
Description: Homemade black and white carrot cake is served. The black one with dark soya sauce is crispy and tasty.

Address: #01-02, 36 Purvis Street, 188613, Singapore
Description: Ossobuco, costoletta alla Milanese and tiramisu are some of the signature dishes here, at one of the city’s best known Italian restaurants. The affable owner, though, wants everyone to be able to find their favourite dish which is why he offers such a large, all-encompassing menu. The impressive wine list, featuring around 7000 labels, is another feature for which this cosy and contemporary-styled restaurant is celebrated.

Address: 20 Ghim Moh Road Market & Food Centre, #01-54, Blk 20, Ghim Moh Road, 270020, Singapore
Description: This stall founded in 1959 is a household name! Its lovingly hand-made chwee kueh – toothsome rice cakes topped with dried radish and mildly spicy sambal – are hugely popular among locals. Minimum order of four pieces.

Address: Marriott Tang Plaza Hotel, #01-04, 320 Orchard Road, 238865, Singapore
Description: The silky smooth and tactile counter was fashioned from a 300-year-old cypress and the wooden ornaments on the wall were handmade by a famous carpenter in Nara. Traditional Edomae sushi is made with seasonal seafood and vegetables from Japan. Only the best rice, marinated with red or white vinegar, makes it to the counter. Even the sauces are shipped from their flagship store in Japan to maintain consistency. The omakase menu is recommended.

Address: Goodwood Park Hotel, 22 Scotts Road, 228221, Singapore
Description: A feature of Goodwood Park hotel since 1963, the restaurant is famed for its meat trolley service which is wheeled over to each table. Along with the meat and plentiful supplies of seafood from the grill, you can expect French-inspired classic dishes like lobster bisque, braised beef cheek, or Crêpes Suzette flambéed tableside. It’s a good choice for a quiet business lunch, a romantic dinner or weekend family outings.

Address: #01-03, 36 Purvis Street, 188613, Singapore
Description: This owner-chef worked in some famous restaurants in his native Belgium and France before coming to Singapore. He describes his cooking as "simple, honest and down-to-earth", though a number of sumptuous dishes are to be had. Try his cold angel hair with a 6g quenelle of Oscietra caviar – one of his proudest creations, served since 2005. In addition to the timeless classics, check out seasonal offerings such as white asparagus.

Restaurant Name: Hai Nan Xing Zhou Beef Noodle
Address: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-06, 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, 310022, Singapore
Description: Choose between blanched rice noodles tossed in a thick gravy, or soup noodles in a deeply flavourful ox bone broth. Then top with sliced beef, beef tripe, tendon, beef balls, or a combination.

Address: Chong Pang Market and Food Centre, #01-129, 105 Yishun Ring Road, 760105, Singapore
Description: Singaporean food such as oyster omelettes, fried prawn mee and carrot cakes. Fried kway teow with cockles and Chinese sausage are cooked-to-order.

Address: 58 Tras Street, 078997, Singapore
Description: Sourcing the finest ingredients is something of an obsession for Kyoto-born Kazuhiro Hamamoto. It's not just his nigiri, whether nodoguro or chutoro, that show his careful craftsmanship – the preceding dishes, such as the uni or smoked tuna course, prove just as memorable. Fish is paired with sushi rice dressed in either red or rice vinegar to accentuate its natural flavours. There is just one sitting at lunch and one at dinner, so book well ahead.

Address: Amoy Street Food Centre, #02-129, 7 Maxwell Road, 069111, Singapore
Description: There is always a queue at this stall famous for umami-laden soup made with mackerel. Enjoy the soup on its own, or use it as a rich base for porridge or bee hoon with sliced fish or fish head. Come early to beat the crowd.

Address: 104 Amoy Street, 069924, Singapore
Description: Hayop serves modern Filipino fare in a wood-rich space with a subtle maritime theme, a reference to the country's fishing industry. The signature dish is Wagyu and watermelon sinigang, a tangy broth with fall-off-the-bone braised beef short ribs – best enjoyed with steamed rice. Pre-order the roast suckling pig 48 hours ahead; known as "lechon de leche", it is copious enough for a few to share. Try their Asian-inspired fruity cocktails, too.

Address: Newton Food Centre, #01-28, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, 229495, Singapore
Description: The owner has 50+ years-experience serving sweet and savoury carrot cakes. Fried oysters and oyster omelettes are also worth a try.

Restaurant Name: Heng Gi Goose and Duck Rice
Address: Tekka Centre, #01-335, 665 Buffalo Road, 210665, Singapore
Description: The soya sauce duck is very popular.

Address: Yuhua Village Market and Food Centre, #01-12, Blk 254, Jurong East Street 24, 600254, Singapore
Description: Both the laksa and prawn mee are made to order and come in three sizes. Their hallmark laksa is doused in a rich aromatic broth and topped with prawns, fried fish cake, fried tofu and cockles.

Address: Hong Lim Market and Food Centre, #01-58, Blk 531A, Upper Cross Street, 051531, Singapore
Description: This stall, founded in the 1970s, is now run by the second-generation owner. Its hallmark dishes are mild, well-balanced curry broth, custom-made tofu puffs and fish cakes, as well as generous helpings of velvety chicken.

Address: Mei Ling Market & Food Centre, #02-42, 159 Mei Chin Road, 140159, Singapore
Description: The BBQ chicken rice is an absolute must, but the honey-glazed char siew and roast pork are also popular. Or opt for their brine-poached chicken – succulent, perfectly seasoned and with a wonderful velvety texture.

Address: Pasar 16@Bedok (Bedok South Food Centre), #01-41, 16 Bedok South Road, 460016, Singapore
Description: This stall serves a single dish that is drop-dead perfect every time. Full-bodied wok hei, irresistible aromas and generous toppings like cockles, Chinese sausage, chives and bean sprouts justify the often hour-long wait.

Restaurant Name: Hill Street Tai Hwa Pork Noodle
Address: Blk 466, #01-12, Crawford Lane, 190466, Singapore
Description: Noodles are cooked-to-order with nicely layered flavours and textures in every bite. Crispy dried plaice, fluffy cracklings, and tender pork liver are all meticulously prepared. Expect to queue any time of the day.

Restaurant Name: Hock Hai (Hong Lim) Curry Chicken Noodle
Address: Bedok Interchange Hawker Centre, #01-58, 208 New Upper Changi Road, 460208, Singapore
Description: The curry broth may be only mildly hot, but its flavours are deep. The chicken is tender; potato and tofu puffs soak up the sauces. Besides curry, there is satay chicken served on your choice from three varieties of noodles.

Restaurant Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Address: Pasar 16@Bedok (Bedok South Food Centre), #01-50, 16 Bedok South Road, 460016, Singapore
Description: Fish balls are tender and rich. The al dente noodles marry well with the fresh broth.

Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-39, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
Description: There is always a queue at this popular stall. Steamed chicken rice with tender meat and flavourful rice perfumed with chicken oil is the must-try. Char siew and roasted pork are also good – order a combo of either.

Address: Blk 19, Toa Payoh 7, #01-264, Kim Keat Palm, 310019, Singapore
Description: As its name suggests, this stall specialises in Hokkien fried noodles in a garlicky broth made with prawn heads. Besides the typical toppings of prawns and squid, you may order others, like egg or abalone, at an additional cost.

Address: Hong Lim Market and Food Centre, #01-66, Blk 531A, Upper Cross Street, 051531, Singapore
Description: The dark amber coloured bak kut teh from this stall is loaded in herbal goodness. Pair with pork knuckle, pork intestines, steamed fish, pork tail, pork kidney or pork liver on the side, as you prefer.

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Address: Tiong Bahru Market, #02-01, 30 Seng Poh Road, 168898, Singapore
Description: Cooked-to-order, the noodles stir-fried with sliced fish, squid and prawn and served with homemade chilli sauce is a favourite.

Address: Alexandra Village Food Centre, #01-51, Blk 120 Bukit Merah Lane 1, 150120, Singapore
Description: Offers six kinds of soups, like lotus root pork ribs & winter melon pork ribs. Also try steamed pork patty with pumpkin or steamed spare ribs.

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Address: People's Park Complex Food Centre, #01-1064, 32 New Market Road, 050032, Singapore
Description: Offers xiao long bao, dumplings and hand-pulled noodles.

Address: Beauty World Food Centre #04-20, 144 Upper Bukit Timah Road, 588177, Singapore
Description: In operation for over half a century, this stall is now run by the second-generation owner and his wife. Their signature soup comprises mutton, tripe or tendon in a garlicky and peppery broth with strong herbal accents.

Address: Amoy Street Food Centre, #01-18, 7 Maxwell Road, 069111, Singapore
Description: Glutinous rice mixed with salted duck egg yolk pork and chestnut wrapped with bamboo leaf.

Address: 51 Old Airport Road Food Centre, #01-35, 51 Old Airport Road, 390051, Singapore
Description: The traditional wanton here is generously filled with pork, either blanched and served in noodle soup or deep-fried. The noodles, cooked to order, boast bouncy texture. The yellow shrimp broth is loaded with flavour.

Address: Yuhua Market & Hawker Centre, #01-171, Blk 347, Jurong East Avenue 1, Jurong East, 600347, Singapore
Description: Bak kut teh with a strong, peppery flavour and aromatic pork ribs. Add rice, pork organs, pork trotter, or vegetable soup for a complete meal.

Address: Whampoa Makan Place, #01-26, 90/91 Whampoa Drive 90, 320091, Singapore
Description: The oyster omelette is fried to order until the crust is nicely browned, while the oysters remain plump and juicy. The house-made chilli sauce elevates the dish considerably. Various portion sizes are available.

Address: Geylang Bahru Market & Food Centre, #01-58, 69 Geylang Bahru, 330069, Singapore
Description: Bouncy ribbon noodles made at the stall are served in soup or "dry" – tossed in house-made chilli sauce and topped with minced meat, meatballs, poached egg and fried lard. With limited availability, they tend to sell out early.

Address: Yuhua Village Market and Food Centre, #01-51, Blk 254, Jurong East Street 24, 600254, Singapore
Description: The queue to get your roasted or boiled chicken rice may be long, but the wait is worthwhile for the silky-fleshed meat and the heady aromas of rice cooked in chicken stock and fat. Enjoy with char siew or roast pork.

Address: Mei Ling Market & Food Centre, #02-38, 159 Mei Chin Road, 140159, Singapore
Description: This popular stall is always busy, even at off-peak times. There are different noodles to choose from, and these are topped with tasty fish balls, pork balls and fried fish cakes. A little of the hot sauce goes a long way!

Address: Claymore Connect, #01-16/17, 442 Orchard Road, 238879, Singapore
Description: After working in a kappo restaurant in Tokyo and helming a famous sushiya in Singapore, Chef Eno has brought to life her own fine-dining concept. At this address since 2024, she serves two set menus that change with the seasons. Her signature somen with kuruma ebi and uni bursts with seafood umami – the briny and sweet prawn broth clings nicely to the silky noodles. Reservations recommended, especially for the sought-after counter seats.

Address: voco Orchard, Level 3, 581 Orchard Road, 238883, Singapore
Description: A picture window in this elegantly furnished room gives diners a front-row view of the kitchen team in action. The tasting menu served at dinner features multiple courses that showcase top-notch produce from Japan and France, such as Miyazaki Wagyu and Bresse pigeon, deftly crafted with European techniques. There is also a plant-based menu for vegans. With thousands of labels from Burgundy, the wine list is worth perusing.

Address: ION Orchard, #03-05, 2 Orchard Turn, 238801, Singapore
Description: Since 2016, this restaurant has been serving traditional Teochew fare with an emphasis on fresh seafood. Only 15 oversized swimmer crabs are steamed and served chilled each day, so order ahead to avoid disappointment. Teochew-style, chilled, steamed fish also impresses with irresistible briny-sweetness, tender flesh and buttery belly. Dip in the delicious Puning bean sauce for extra umami. Other classics, like the oyster omelette, are also worth trying.

Address: Paragon Shopping Centre, #05-42/45, 290 Orchard Road, 238859, Singapore
Description: Considered the crown jewel of the group, this place stocks over 3 000 Peking ducks a month, yet still tends to sell out, so be sure to pre-order yours when booking your table. The restaurant is divided into three rooms and the roasted duck – a must-try with crispy skin and succulent meat – is carved tableside. Another signature dish is the velvety poached fish in shrimp stock on crispy rice; the roast pork and slow-boiled soups are also worth trying.

Address: 35 Scotts Road, 228227, Singapore
Description: Dark wood furniture and antiques add to the elegant colonial spirit of this restaurant nestled in a bungalow, also known as ‘The White House’. The menu offers Peranakan cuisine and the dishes look deceptively simple, but involve subtly blended spices and seasoning. Wagyu beef rendang uses the cheek cut for tenderness, while spices, fermented shrimp paste, chilli and coconut milk underscore the rich, deep flavour.

Address: 49 Tras Street, 078988, Singapore
Description: Outfitted with marble flooring, leather banquettes and dark wood panelling, this place exudes warmth and sleekness. The owner-chef imbues European fare with creative twists in a menu that features fermented foods, chargrilled dishes and an array of meats aged in-house. When grilling carabineros, he throws in some beef fat to accentuate the richness of the tomalley, and his truffle brioche is paired with miso vinegar for deep, earthy umami.

Address: 27 Scotts Road, 228222, Singapore
Description: A Singaporean chef and his Taiwanese wife opened this restaurant with 12 counter seats and a private room serving authentic Taiwanese fare using top-notch ingredients from the island. The chef’s creative vision and solid skills shine through in tiny details and subtle flavours. His kamameshi rice in a cast iron pot features seasonal catch from the sea and Taiwanese rice. Crispy, smoky rice on the bottom works magically with the fish and house-made pickles.

Address: Raffles Arcade, #01-11, 328 North Bridge Road, 188719, Singapore
Description: This exclusive nine-seater in a prestigious hotel is helmed by experienced chef Takahiro Ishizawa. Informed by stints in some celebrated sushi-ya, he breaks away from his previous recipes to explore a new approach that truly reflects his vision. The four set menus served at dinner feature rice from Akita dressed in a unique blend of vinegars, and the freshest catch flown in from Japan four times a week. Reservations are a must.

Address: Pasir Panjang Food Centre, #14, 121 Pasir Panjang Road, 118543, Singapore
Description: Herbal mutton soup, herbal tendon soup and herbal tulang soup are delicious.

Address: Amoy Street Food Centre, #01-21, 7 Maxwell Road, 069111, Singapore
Description: The curry puff comes in four flavours, all wrapped in a flaky, crispy pastry crust. As well as the classic chicken and potato curry, try the black pepper chicken, sweet taro or chilli sardine-filled pastry.

Address: Swissôtel The Stamford, Equinox Complex, Level 70, 2 Stamford Road, 178882, Singapore
Description: Embodying the essence of fine dining, this romantic restaurant has it all – wonderful food, service and ambiance, and spectacular views. Chef Westaway makes good use of top-notch British produce and inspirations to turn out modern culinary creations that never fail to impress. A British classic, fish & chips, gets a posh makeover with sour cream, lemon zest and caviar. Even the alcohol-free gin and tonic palate cleanser is impeccably crafted.

Address: Forum The Shopping Mall, #B1-13, 583 Orchard Road, 238884, Singapore
Description: Both the décor and the menu show strong Hong Kong influences, all the more so as super-fresh seafood and veggies are shipped from the city twice a week. The must-tries (sautéed white eel with chives in black bean sauce and braised lobster with ginger and scallion in a claypot) boast exceptional wok hei and craftsmanship. You can also specify how you want your live seafood cooked – ask the friendly front-of-house staff for advice.

Address: 2 Jalan Ayer, Lorong 1 Geylang, 389141, Singapore
Description: In operation for over 70 years, this place serves aromatic dry prawn mee in sambal with heaps of fried scallion and depth. The soup version has a prawn broth loaded with natural umami. Choose from three kinds of noodles.

Address: ABC Brickworks Market & Food Centre, #01-112, Blk 6 Jalan Bukit Merah, 150006, Singapore
Description: Besides Penangese quick bites from char kway teow to prawn mee, this stall is famous for Penang assam laksa – the tangy, mildly hot yellowtail fish broth works magic with the noodles; but it's the fresh mint that makes it so distinctive.

Restaurant Name: Ji De Lai Hainanese Chicken Rice
Address: Chong Pang Market and Food Centre, #01-152, 105 Yishun Ring Road, 760105, Singapore
Description: Hainanese chicken rice comes with options like roasted or steamed chicken. Sets with rice, soup and vegetables are reasonably priced.

Address: Hong Lim Market and Food Centre, #02-48/49, Blk 531A, Upper Cross Street, 051531, Singapore
Description: Order the Ji Ji noodle bowl – noodle soup or ‘dry’ noodles are topped with char siew, deep-fried wonton and veggies and served with wonton soup. Pork crackling adds a lovely crunch. A dab of homemade chilli sauce is a must.

Address: Tiong Bahru Market, #02-05, 30 Seng Poh Road, 168898, Singapore
Description: Shui kueh is quintessential local street food: white rice cake with salted diced radish and a secret tung tsai sauce, packed with oomph. The house-made sambal, oozing in dried shrimp flavour, is perfect with the rice cake.

Restaurant Name: Jian Bo Tiong Bahru Shui Kueh (Jurong West)
Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-27, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
Description: The rice cake with a sauce of preserved vegetables, sesame, dried shrimp and chilli is spicy and delicious.

Address: Four Seasons Hotel, Level 2, 190 Orchard Boulevard, 248646, Singapore
Description: This exquisite space, reached via a marble staircase, is warm and welcoming, with heavy leather chairs that are especially comfortable. The kitchen team excels in barbecue meats, double-boiled soups and seafood dishes that use the freshest ingredients of the best quality. Try wok-fried Australian beef tenderloin with portobello mushrooms. Set menus are a great way to sample the popular hits all at once.

Address: Yishun Park Hawker Centre, #01-39, 51 Yishun Avenue 11, 768867, Singapore
Description: Cooked-to-order seafood dishes. Signature sambal stingray is spicy and delicious.

Address: 51 Old Airport Road Food Centre, #01-120, 51 Old Airport Road, 390051, Singapore
Description: Come here for flavourful made-to-order grouper broth with milk added for extra creaminess. Try the soup on its own or with bee hoon, sliced fish, fried fish meat and fried fish head. The spicy bean sauce and deep-fried shallot work magic with the broth.

Address: Marina Bay Sands Hotel, Tower 1, Level 55, 10 Bayfront Avenue, 018956, Singapore
Description: Perched atop the iconic Marina Bay Sands Hotel, the room affords gorgeous city and harbour views. Gold trim nicely contrasts with the muted dark blue walls in the Song Dynasty-inspired interior. Chef Albert Li is famous for his refined Cantonese fare, such as roasted pipa duck with black pepper sauce – the bird is deboned, minced and stuffed back into its own skin before being roasted to perfection. The predominantly Chinese wine list includes some rare gems.

Address: Blk 349, #01-1215 Jurong East Avenue 1, 600349, Singapore
Description: The signature dish here is pepper-flavoured bak kut teh. The soft pork rib goes well with chilli soy sauce. Earlier closing hours on Sunday.

Address: 10 Ann Siang Hill, 069789, Singapore
Description: The simple, cosy space with exposed beams and wooden furnishings exudes a warm feel. Balancing sweet, sour and salty notes with fiery heat, the chef turns fresh produce into modern Thai dishes that are packed with flavour. The small menu changes regularly but may include signatures such as smoky chargrilled pork jowl, or yellow crab curry with beautifully bold aromas. The friendly and dynamic service team is also a plus.

Address: 2/4 Keong Saik Road, 089112, Singapore
Description: For over 50 years, Kok Sen has been feeding hungry diners with cze char classics, such as their stir-fries boasting exceptional wok hei. Look out for the colourful lightboxes with signature items like prawn paste chicken or fish cooked in various ways. Seating may be a bit cramped, but the round tables and green booth seats work well with a grey colour scheme and pale wood. Given the small number of tables, expect to queue.

Address: Wilkie Edge, #01-23/24, 8 Wilkie Road, 228095, Singapore
Description: After helming a renowned sushiya in Singapore for 10 years, chef Yukinori Kawakami has brought his experience to Sushi Yuki. Omakase and kaiseki set menus, at different price points, feature fish flown in from Japan four times a week. Sushi rice from Yamagata Prefecture is dressed in a blend of two vinegars for a delicate taste that accentuates the natural flavours of the fish. There are just 13 counter seats and two private rooms, so booking is recommended.

Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-29, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
Description: Although the menu also offers laksa, pork balls and fish dumpling soup, the bouncy, flavoursome fishballs with noodles remain its speciality. Choose between wheat or rice noodles, served in a clear broth or tossed in sauces.

Address: Zion Riverside Food Centre, #06, 70 Zion Road, 247792, Singapore
Description: Alongside wanton or dumpling noodle soup, this stall serves deep-fried wanton and char siew. The springy noodles are best enjoyed with a dollop of chilli sauce, while the wantons encase a tasty filling in their paper-thin skin.

Restaurant Name: Kelantan Kway Chap Pig's Organ Soup
Address: Berseh Food Centre, #02-39, 166 Jalan Besar, 208877, Singapore
Description: Pork cuts and offal like belly, trotter, intestines and skin are cooked in a soy-based marinade with spices. The depth and rich flavours of the meat are the perfect accompaniment to the kway chap ribbon noodles.

Address: Blk 124, #01-136, Bukit Merah Lane 1, 150124, Singapore
Description: This popular cze char restaurant may not be the most conveniently placed, but it does some great dishes, like fried salted egg crab, coffee pork ribs and claypot duck with sea cucumber. The setting and environment are not unlike a hawker centre, although there is a smaller inside area that’s air-conditioned. It provides mostly Hainanese cuisine, along with some Cantonese dishes – the stir-fries are particularly delicious.

Address: #01-01, 60 Tras Street, 078999, Singapore
Description: In a minimalistic room, the Taiwanese owner-chef serves an omakase menu of creative vegetarian courses in which Japanese and French culinary traditions converge. Modern cooking techniques like sous vide are used to imbue plant-based ingredients with meaty flavours and textures. Smoked capsicum and pumpkin purée are made to look like akami and uni in their nigiri sushi. The menu changes regularly to keep it fresh.

Address: CT Hub, #01-08/13, 2 Kallang Avenue, 339407, Singapore
Description: The Malaysian owner opened this simple shop in 2024, specialising in authentic nasi lemak, often considered the national dish of his home country. The chef, who is also Malaysian, cooks rice in coconut milk with pandan leaves, and garnishes it with fried anchovies, peanuts, fried egg, sliced cucumber and spicy sambal. For a substantial meal, add sides such as ayam berempah (fried chicken leg), rendang chicken or ayam kunyit (turmeric chicken).

Address: Tiong Bahru Market, #02-29, 30 Seng Poh Road, 168898, Singapore
Description: Pork offal like tripe and liver is served with meatballs and sliced pork in a peppery broth with pickled mustard greens. Dip the pork into chilli sauce for an extra kick. Also try the sticky rice sausage stuffed with pork belly and chestnuts.

Address: North Bridge Road Market & Food Centre, #01-99, 861 North Bridge Road, 198783, Singapore
Description: Barbecue pork with wonton noodles is the signature. Deep-fried pork skin and chillies enrich the flavour.

Address: New Bahru, #01-03, 46 Kim Yam Road, 239351, Singapore
Description: Moved to this spot in 2024, Kotuwa is named after the CBD of Colombo. From quintessential Sri Lankan street food to curries, every bite is loaded with big flavours. Seafood is their strong suit, especially crab prepared in myriad ways. With its balanced, layered flavours and the subtle warmth of cinnamon, the crab curry really stands out. Hoppers – crispy pancakes made with fermented rice – are perfect for mopping up the delicious curry sauce.

Address: Newton Food Centre, #01-20, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, 229495, Singapore
Description: Fish porridge and fried fish bee hoon. The porridge is sweet with abundant fish fillets.

Address: Newton Food Centre, #01-13, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, 229495, Singapore
Description: With over 40 years of history, Kwee Heng makes boneless braised duck that is tender, juicy and flavoursome; it can be served with rice, congee or noodles. Other dishes such as Hainanese chicken and char siew are also available.

Address: Mercure ICON Hotel, #01-08, 8 Club Street, 069472, Singapore
Description: This 150-year-old Neapolitan pizza chain opened their first Asian outpost in 2024 and offers 18 different toppings. All the pizzas are made to order and come in one size only – 15 inches (37cm). Piled high with freshly cooked tomato sauce and cheese, the thin crust is perfectly crisp and chewy at the same time. If you can’t make up your mind, opt for a Marita – half marinara half margherita. The menu also offers starters, pasta and desserts.

Address: Mandarin Gallery, #01-16/17, 333A Orchard Road, 238897, Singapore
Description: Hailing from Tokyo, Japan, chef-owner Sasaki honed his skills in Italy. His ambitious kappo-style cooking effortlessly blends Italian traditions with Japanese influences, delivering complex, original creations underpinned by modern techniques. His signature Hokkaido uni pasta seduces with its silky sauce; shavings of Sardinian bottarga add extra umami. Besides fixed à la carte choices, there is a regularly changing tasting menu to reflect seasonality.

Address: 6 Upper Dickson Road, 207466, Singapore
Description: You can specify the level of spiciness of your food at this three-storey restaurant in Little India, though many come for the Chilli Challenge on full moon nights simply to push their limit. But spiciness isn’t all that this chef has to offer – in fact, he balances it with sweet, sour, salty, bitter and astringent flavours. Choose between table seating downstairs and floor seating upstairs. Parties of two have a number of set menus to choose from.

Address: Yuhua Market & Hawker Centre, #01-218, Blk 347, Jurong East Avenue 1, Jurong East, 600347, Singapore
Description: Handmade Teochew kueh with various flavours. Steamed or pan-fried versions available.

Restaurant Name: Lao Fu Zi Fried Kway Teow
Address: 51 Old Airport Road Food Centre, #01-12, 51 Old Airport Road, 390051, Singapore
Description: Fried kway teow comes in two portion sizes and black and white varieties. Both feature good wok hei and silky texture. Bean sprouts, egg, preserved sausage and blood clams provide extra flavours.

Address: Mei Ling Market & Food Centre, #02-15, 159 Mei Chin Road, 140159, Singapore
Description: Cantonese-style noodles topped with beef brisket, pork ribs, pork knuckles or beef tendon are the name of the game here. The noodles are springy, and the pork knuckles are braised until gelatinous in a secret soy sauce.

Address: 40 Tras Street, 078979, Singapore
Description: Chef Arévalo reinvents the traditional cuisine of his home country with modern, playful twists. His new spin on authentic Colombian flavours makes his dishes approachable even for first-timers. The arepa de chócolo y huevo – corn cake filled with eggs and grilled pork jowl – has a more mellow taste than the version typically served in his homeland. The bright room adorned with Colombian tribal art and masks exudes a cheerful, convivial vibe.

Address: Chijmes, #01-24, 30 Victoria Street, 187996, Singapore
Description: Unlike other branches in the group, this one has a European décor echoing the colonial style of the building that hosts it. That said, the menu remains the same as the others. Apart from the main menu, make sure you check out the chef’s selection menu. Double-boiled soups, flavourful and hearty, are unmissable. Deep-fried spare ribs marinated with shrimp paste are crispy and loaded with umami.

Restaurant Name: Leon Kee Claypot Pork Rib Soup
Address: Alexandra Village Food Centre, #01-18, Blk 120 Bukit Merah Lane 1, 150120, Singapore
Description: The pork rib soup cooked with Chinese herbs is the signature dish; it also offers pig's tail soup, sesame oil chicken and claypot pork liver.

Address: 7 Mohamed Sultan Road, 238957, Singapore
Description: Sporting a brand-new image, Lerouy moved to this new address in 2024. Head to the cute little bar for a pre- or post-meal drink. The main dining area overlooks the open kitchen for a chef’s table-like vibe. As always, the food is served omakase style – choose the number of courses and tell the servers about your allergies and dislikes. The kitchen excels in unexpected food and flavour combinations that never fail to pleasantly surprise.

Address: Shaw Centre, #01-16, 1 Scotts Road, 228208, Singapore
Description: Haute cuisine is increasingly about the chef embracing creative freedom and dictating the whole experience. At the longstanding, singularly sophisticated and world-renowned Les Amis, the choice is yours. The prix-fixe menus present a wide range of modern French classics with occasional Asian twists, in which simple ingredient combinations and seasoning highlight the natural flavours. Consider booking the chef's table for an intimate experience.

Address: 8 Ann Siang Hill, 069788, Singapore
Description: After some years in Singapore, the French owner-chef opened Les Ducs to honour the traditions of French cuisine. Expect authentic classics – from bouillabaisse to pâté en croute au foie gras – that showcase well-honed techniques and quality fresh ingredients. The Australian beef tenderloin with black pepper sauce boasts tender, juicy meat, and the flavours are spot on. Predominantly French, the wine list is also worth perusing. The lunch sets are great value.

Address: Chinatown Complex Market & Food Centre, #02-198/199, 335 Smith Street, 050335, Singapore
Description: It takes 30 minutes to cook but is more than worth the wait. The rice, cooked in a claypot over charcoal, exudes smokiness with a crispy scorched crust on the bottom. For toppings, choose between chicken, preserved pork and/or sausage.

Address: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-20, Blk 19 Toa Payoh Lor 7, 310019, Singapore
Description: The owner makes the fish balls by hand to ensure they are springy and bursting with umami. Blanched noodles tossed in chilli sauce with crispy cracklings are the perfect companion to the fish ball soup.

Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-185, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
Description: The signature wonton noodles feature flavoursome bite-size dumplings, served either in soup or tossed in sauces. The noodles are cooked to perfect consistency with a lovely chew. Sliced char siew adds depth.

Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-31, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
Description: Serve yourself with the stuffed tofu or vegetables. You may also add soup, chee cheong fun, laksa, mee or rice.

Address: 237 Lorong 9 Geylang, 389296, Singapore
Description: Cantonese and Fujian dishes prepared with local ingredients are tweaked to cater to local tastes. The beef kway teow is the main event. Comfort-food classics such as coffee pork ribs and sambal sweet potato leaves are also excellent.

Address: Tiong Bahru Market, #02-23, 30 Seng Poh Road, 168898, Singapore
Description: The rich, robust stock that clings to the egg noodles is the secret behind their tasty lor mee. Deep-fried fish nuggets, pork, and bean sprouts also make every bite satisfying. Grated garlic and cilantro add a zesty boost.

Address: 22 Gemmill Lane, 069257, Singapore
Description: A favourite with local office workers, this steakhouse and oyster bar, run by a U.S. national, bustles with patrons all day long and is ideal for power lunches or after-work cocktails. It has acquired a faithful crowd of regulars thanks to high-quality food and friendly, slick service. Expect to see U.S. classics on the menu, such as New England clam chowder and Maryland crab cake. The generous portions make it a great venue for get-togethers.

Address: Vision Exchange, #02-41/42, 2 Venture Drive, 608526, Singapore
Description: This simple shop may not be the most atmospheric, but its tasty food in generous portions at affordable prices always attracts a crowd. With a Thai owner and all Thai kitchen team, rest assured that the food is as authentic as can be. The tom yum soup strikes a fine balance between sour, sweet, spicy and salty tastes; the BBQ squid is nicely grilled and loaded with umami, perfect with the hot and sour sauce. Reservation recommended.

Address: 38 Craig Road, 089676, Singapore
Description: Candles in wine bottles and tables made from wine barrels are among the details that set the authentic small bistro scene here. Wine connoisseurs will be bowled over by the wine cellar and knowledgeable servers, who know every vintage inside out. Classic French recipes are made with local ingredients to cater to the local palate. Many dishes are meant to share, making this lively spot a great place for get-togethers.

Address: #01-88, 57 Eng Hoon Street, 160057, Singapore
Description: With mosaic tile flooring, warm wood tones and vintage knickknacks, the interior feels relaxing and modern; meanwhile, the patio beneath a canopy is perfect for al fresco dining. The chef champions borderless cuisine, melding eclectic influences from around the world – Indian, Chinese, European, LatAm and even Fijian touches feature in his ingenious creations that work like a charm. Try the tandoori bread with butter spread perfumed by citrus and pepper aromas.

Address: The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands, #B1-15 & L1-83, 10 Bayfront Avenue, 018956, Singapore
Description: Located in the shopping mall at Marina Bay Sands, Maison Boulud features a patio on the upper level – boasting stunning views, it is perfect for al fresco dining. The elegant main space (lower level) has an oversized wine cellar displaying impressive vintages. Classic French cuisine, with more sophisticated plating, dominates the menu, but they also have a signature seafood platter, plus dishes infused with Asian touches, such as durian "royale" soufflé.

Address: Marina One, The Heart (East Tower) #04-01, 5 Straits View, 018935, Singapore
Description: Laid out beneath a glass roof, the airy dining area overlooks a garden. The food, which draws on modern techniques and time-honoured traditions, is exquisite in both taste and appearance. The claypot chicken with glutinous rice wine, ginger and wood ear fungus boasts silky, free-range meat and spellbinding aromas. The business clientele can opt for items in individual servings. Booking a week ahead recommended.

Restaurant Name: Margaret Drive Sin Kee Chicken Rice
Address: Block 40, Stall 5, #01-39, Holland Drive, 270040, Singapore
Description: Since this stall opened on Margaret Drive years ago, their chicken rice has been made the same way. The juicy, tender meat is served with aromatic oil rice and an addictive ground ginger sauce. The gizzards are equally good.

Address: Flower Dome, #01-09, Gardens by The Bay, 18 Marina Gardens Drive, 018953, Singapore
Description: Dining in the Flower Dome makes for a back-to-nature moment and Chef Wilson does it with a touch of class. In his tasting menu, gracefully presented courses are underpinned by solid techniques, packed with oomph and flavours bold enough to match the showy, colourful blooms. The wine list showcases some rare labels, including bottles from Lebanon and Morocco, while the temperance pairing is also interesting. Service is seamless and personable.

Address: Maxwell Food Centre, #01-05, 1 Kadayanallur Street, 069184, Singapore
Description: The second-generation owner still fries oyster cakes à la minute as her mother did in the 1960s. They may be darker than usual, but the minced pork, oysters, prawns and coriander are still soft and juicy under the crispy crust.

Address: Block 232, #01-1222, Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3, 560232, Singapore
Description: It may not be in the most convenient location but that doesn’t deter the crowds from descending on this open-air space. Nearly everyone is here for one thing: crab. The chef has 15 different ways to cook them, from black pepper crab to creamy butter crab and that, of course, includes the classic chilli crab. There’s also live seafood available, along with cze char dishes – and the claypot bee hoon soup is delicious.

Address: 9 Mohamed Sultan Road, 238959, Singapore
Description: Chef Sun Kim hails from Korea's Busan and his refined modern cooking combines Korean traditions and bold flavours with minimalist plating. The single tasting menu is dominated by seafood and vegetables, as seen in steamed Jeju abalone with gochujang seaweed risotto – the tender mollusc, creamy rice and crunchy lily bulbs feature contrasting textures. In addition to wine pairing, the non-alcoholic Korean drink flight is also worth trying.

Address: 7A & 7B Dempsey Road, 249684, Singapore
Description: Amidst lush greenery, the one-storey colonial structure houses an airy dining room done up in a yellow, gold and green palette, boasting floor-to-ceiling windows, wood details and rattan furniture. The menu is Cantonese and Sichuanese with a touch of finesse and subtlety. Must-try items include turbot fish two ways, Beijing duck grilled in a wood-fire oven and various dim sum. There are also many good choices for vegetarians.

Address: 75 Brighton Crescent, 559216, Singapore
Description: Before you can experience the head chef’s unique take on Singaporean-Japanese fusion cooking, you have to book a table online months ahead. Punctuality is key as the food is only served after all the guests are seated at 7:30pm sharp. The 8- or 9-course omakase-style menu changes every two months, reinventing national dishes like rojak and laksa with clever Japanese twists. Everything is served by the chefs, who take the time to explain each dish.

Restaurant Name: Mustard Singapore - Flavours of Bengal & Punjab
Address: 32 Race Course Road, 218552, Singapore
Description: This halal restaurant specialising in Bengali and Punjabi cuisines is christened Mustard because the spice is used extensively in both cuisines. For instance, mustard oil is often used in place of coconut oil in Bengali cooking. Try their maacher cutlet – deep-fried fish croquettes served with a house-made fermented mustard sauce called Kashundi, which tastes strong and spicy. All food is made to order, but is so worth the wait.

Address: #01-01, 138 Race Course Road, 218591, Singapore
Description: ‘Muthu’ means pearl in Tamil, which befits this gem (with another branche) serving traditional dishes from both the Southern and Northern regions of India. Originally called Muthu Makkan, the owner expanded and renamed the restaurant in 1982. The signature fish head, South Indian-style, uses a secret blend of spices. Swimmer crabs, masala prawns, lamb rack and tandoori chicken are also big hits among diners. Ask about the monthly specials.

Address: 115 Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre, #01-47, Blk 115 Bukit Merah View, 151115, Singapore
Description: The fish head curry with eggplant, okra and tofu puff stands out with its aromatic spice paste made from scratch, paired with a hint of coconut milk. The fish, lamb and chicken curry are also popular.

Address: Hyundai Motor Group Innovation Center Singapore, Level 3, 2 Bulim Link, 649674, Singapore
Description: The joint venture between a motor group and Korean-American chef Corey Lee advocates a ‘seed to table’ concept, whereby most of the veggies served are picked every morning from the ‘smart’ farm abutting the dining room. The combination of Korean culinary traditions and cutting-edge technology is quite inspiring. The kitchen of mostly Korean natives delivers a single seasonal tasting menu of refined Korean dishes.

Address: 161 Telok Ayer Street, 068615, Singapore
Description: The bright room is furnished in a cream and birch colour scheme, imparting calmness and warmth. The Korean chef Louis Han named his restaurant Nae:um, meaning a fragrance that evokes memories. Food culture and recollections of his home country are at the core of his episodic menu that changes with seasons. Innovative courses are precisely executed and presented in an ethereal, refreshing manner, but have inklings of their Korean roots.

Address: 51 Old Airport Road Food Centre, #01-32, 51 Old Airport Road, 390051, Singapore
Description: This stall has been serving just one item since opening its doors in 1960 – Hokkien fried mee with prawns. The egg noodles and rice vermicelli are tossed in a rich broth made with prawn shells and tomalley to impart deep umami.

Address: Yishun Park Hawker Centre, #01-33, 51 Yishun Avenue 11, 768867, Singapore
Description: Traditional coconut milk rice with Indonesian spicy chicken and sambal sauce.

Address: National Gallery Singapore, #02-01, (Coleman Street entrance), 1 St. Andrew's Road, 178957, Singapore
Description: Art and sculptures aren’t the only treasures found in the National Gallery – on the 2nd floor is this restaurant from Violet Oon, Singapore’s own national treasure and one of its greatest ambassadors. The handsome, panelled 1920s-style dining room is an ideal backdrop to the cooking which, through its spicing, contrasting textures and enticing aromas, showcases Singapore’s unique culinary heritage. This is a restaurant with genuine charm.

Address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-19, 44 Holland Drive, 270044, Singapore
Description: The claypot rice here is cooked to order over charcoal from scratch; the rice grains are left soft, chewy and separable from each other. The portion size is plenty for two to share. To avoid a long wait, call to pre-order.

Address: Bedok Interchange Hawker Centre, #01-23, 208 New Upper Changi Road, 460208, Singapore
Description: The speciality here – mutton soup – is briny-sweet with plenty of umami, and finely shredded ginger to add zing. Other lamb specialities such as rib soup, kway teow, meatballs, lamb tendon and offal are also worth trying.

Restaurant Name: No.18 Zion Road Fried Kway Teow
Address: Zion Riverside Food Centre, #017, 70 Zion Road, 247792, Singapore
Description: Kway teow noodles are fried to order and topped with fish cake and cockles. The wok hei impresses with its robust flavours and a hint of spiciness, while the cockles impart extra umami. The wait can be long, but is well worth it.

Address: 72 Amoy Street, 069891, Singapore
Description: Championing a concept of “crossroads” cooking, the chef explores how cultures, ingredients, and geographical locations intersect with a menu that unfolds like a narrative. Motifs such as vanilla and turmeric are repeated throughout and lighter flavours build up to a tour-de-force climax. The marble table and conjoining chef’s counter are the preferred front row seats to interact with and watch the chefs work.

Address: Chong Pang Market and Food Centre, #01-162, 105 Yishun Ring Road, 760105, Singapore
Description: The stall specialises in the classic iced dessert chendol. Pandan-flavoured flour jelly, coconut milk and palm sugar syrup impart the right level of sweetness. Extra toppings like red beans or durian are available.

Address: 1 Keong Saik Road, 089109, Singapore
Description: After travelling the world to broaden his culinary know-how, this culinary nomad has decided to settle with Spanish cuisine, but adds bold, exciting global influences – the traditional Mediterranean grilled octopus gets a makeover with Japanese bonito broth. The menu sees tapas rubbing shoulders with dishes to share of the likes of Spanish suckling pig or paella. The relaxed, bustling vibe also adds to the establishment’s appeal.

Address: National Gallery, #01-04, 1 St. Andrew's Road (entrance via Supreme Court wing's foyer), 178957, Singapore
Description: Where better to find a priceless jewel of the Singapore dining scene than in The National Gallery? Chef Julien Royer and his highly accomplished kitchen make wonderful use of luxury ingredients of unimpeachable quality. Creative combinations, impeccable techniques and exquisite plating result in dishes that are as elegant as they are memorable. The understated and graceful room, overseen by a highly polished service team, provides the perfect backdrop.

Address: #01-03, 55 Keong Saik Road, 089158, Singapore
Description: Come to this lively Catalan hotspot for tapas and small plates, which boast delicate handiwork, modern plating and lashings of flavour. Try the 'Segovia' style suckling Iberico pig or ‘A Feira’ octopus – pork belly and octopus in a silky potato foam with caramelised onion. Be sure to save room for their iconic creamy cheesecake. The chic interior by Barcelona-based designer Rosa-Violán embodies the Mediterranean soul, whisking diners instantly off to Spain.

Address: #01-03, 30 Stevens Road, 257840, Singapore
Description: The chef hails from Osaka and honed his skills in some of Tokyo’s top kitchens. In his 6- or 8-course omakase menu, he revisits his Japanese roots with classic French techniques. Exquisite dishes made with quality seasonal Japanese produce taste light, sophisticated and subtle. With only 16 seats at the pine wood counter overlooking the open kitchen, reservations are recommended. The immaculate service further adds to the experience.

Address: 130E Minden Road, 248819, Singapore
Description: Adjacent to the Botanic Garden, this verdantly set glasshouse combines an urban farm and dining concept. The founder-chef advocates an eco-friendly philosophy and therefore designed a mostly plant-based menu. Produce may be sourced from local artisan farms as well as Malaysia, but the food shows eclectic technique and flavours from around the world. The menu offers vegan, vegetarian and gluten-free options to cater to different dietary needs.

Address: Hilton Orchard, Level 5, 333 Orchard Road, 238867, Singapore
Description: After a hiatus, the first Asian outpost of celebrity chef Nancy Silverton’s famed establishment Osteria Mozza reopened, now in a modern, rustic setting with a lively and inviting vibe. The small lunch menu features antipasti, salads, pizza and house-made pasta. The dinner menu steps up a gear to include her signature mozzarella dishes and other Italian specialties. The impressive wine list covers 280 labels from different regions of Italy.

Restaurant Name: Outram Park Fried Kway Teow Mee
Address: Hong Lim Market and Food Centre, #02-17, Blk 531A, Upper Cross Street, 051531, Singapore
Description: The Kway Teow is fried with a dark sauce you can add cockles to the noodles. Always a long queue.

Address: Gallop Entrance, Singapore Botanic Gardens, 11 Gallop Road, 259015, Singapore
Description: The view of the lush green in the garden is one good reason to visit. But owner-chef Malcolm Lee's exquisite tasting menu that explores the untapped possibilities of Straits cuisine is what makes the experience of dining here unforgettable. Named after the plant that produces buah keluak seeds, a key ingredient in Peranakan cuisine, Pangium pays homage to family recipes passed down for generations with carefully crafted dishes that taste exceptional.

Address: People's Park Complex Food Centre, #01-1098, 32 New Market Road, 050032, Singapore
Description: Cantonese barbecue like roast pork and duck aside, the main draws are Hainanese chicken rice and double-boiled soups. The rice is richly perfumed with garlic and the flavourful chicken with a gelatinous skin is not to be missed.

Address: 486 Serangoon Road, 218151, Singapore
Description: The name says it all – this vegetarian joint prides itself on the spicy ground lentil condiment known as podi, and sautéed vegetables, or poriyal. Replicating South Indian grandmas' cooking, the menu covers all plant-based dietary desires, with gluten-free, allium-free and vegan options. "Which Podi? Idli" – steamed rice cake tossed in podi – is served with a cashew and coconut chutney. Their podi dosai with poriyal filling is also excellent.

Restaurant Name: Poh Cheu Soon Kueh and Ang Ku Kueh
Address: Blk 127, KPT Coffee Shop, #01-230, Bukit Merah Lane 1, 150127, Singapore
Description: Ideal for fresh kueh, made from scratch daily. Colourful ang ku kueh comes in 10+ different sweet fillings and the black sesame variety stands out. Savoury kueh with bamboo shoot, yam, or chive filling are also popular.

Address: Albert Centre, #01-123, 270 Queen Street, 180270, Singapore
Description: Among the array of Indonesian food on offer, their grilled-to-order satay stands out in particular. Chicken satay is marinated in turmeric, imparting a mild sweetness; juicy, tender mutton satay is immaculately cooked.

Address: 127 Kitchener Road, 208514, Singapore
Description: This first branch of the chain known for its friendly service opened in 2000. The menu showcases Fujian classics, with small plates and noodles being the highlights. Try the bian rou (Fujian wonton soup) – the translucent skin is made with pork pounded over 10,000 times into a paste. The lor mee, topped with an impressive array of seafood, is also popular. Don't miss the seasonal offerings, some using rare ingredients from the city of Putian.

Address: Artyzen Hotel, Level 4, 9 Cuscaden Road, 249719, Singapore
Description: Supervised by Chef Victor Liong from Melbourne, and helmed by Chef Su, who is of Indian-Chinese descent, this fine dining restaurant serves menus imbued with a deeply rooted multicultural ethos. Australian ingredients are used in conjunction with local produce in pan-Asian recipes that meld Singaporean, Malaysian and Indonesian influences. Expect unmistakably Asian flavours, such as buah keluak and tamarind, in creative, neat culinary gems.

Address: Newton Food Centre, #01-76, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, 229495, Singapore
Description: Chicken wings grilled with charcoal are crispy and juicy while the spicy sauce adds to the flavour. Also try satay, traditional popiah and kueh pie tee.

Address: Tampines Round Market & Food Centre, #01-33, 137 Tampines Street 11, 521137, Singapore
Description: The mother-and-son team serves thosai and appam made from scratch. Their thosai comes in nearly 20 different fillings such as crispy cereal, or cheese, egg and butter – everything tastes better with the sambar and chutney dips.

Address: Redhill Market, #01-90, 85 Redhill Lane, 150085, Singapore
Description: The porridge may not look exciting but the creamy base is loaded with meaty flavour. Pad it out with sliced pork, pork meatballs, pork liver or deep-fried dough sticks. Crack in a raw egg and stir it into wispy ribbons. Open from 6am while stocks lasts.

Address: National Gallery, #01-02A, 1 St. Andrew's Road, 178957, Singapore
Description: In a smart, casual room with tan banquettes, powder blue chairs and terrazzo tiled floor, Damian D’Silva, a respected judge from the Singaporean edition of a popular cooking show, champions a novel cuisine that crosses boundaries among Chinese, Peranakan, Eurasian, Indian and Malay cooking. Hearty dishes sit comfortably next to century-old recipes, all prepared with shrewd judgment, and the right amount of oomph. Baca Assam (beef cheek) is unmissable.

Address: #01-01, 1 Neil Road, 088804, Singapore
Description: Housed in Jinricksha Station, a former rickshaw depot circa 1903, Born boasts a modern dining room adorned by glowing double arches, high glass ceiling and an ethereal paper sculpture. Chef Tan cooks up a 9-course tasting menu inspired by the circle of life and his personal journey, melding French gastronomy with Chinese cooking. Dishes are creative and crafted with globally sourced ingredients, delivering contrasts in textures and flavours.

Address: Level 2, 77 Neil Road, 088903, Singapore
Description: After helming some prestigious kitchens in Singapore, Japanese chef Kawano came up with a 10-course dinner menu that allows diners to appreciate his culinary vision to the fullest. French and Japanese produce is juxtaposed to great effect and finessed by solid French techniques. Dishes are pleasing to the eye as well as the palate. Painstakingly tweaking the consistency of his duck consommé daily, he shows his attention to detail is second to none.

Address: #01-01/02, 21 Tanjong Pagar Road, 088444, Singapore
Description: Malaysian owner-chef Hafizzul Hashim opened Fiz in 2023 to honour his native food culture. In addition to à la carte dishes and the vegetarian set, consider ordering his ‘full experience’ menu – an ode to his childhood with family recipes that pack a punch. The food is intricately crafted with Malaysian produce, and the main courses are served communal style to re-enact traditions. Also try the house cocktails and wine-food pairings.

Address: 18 North Canal Road, 048830, Singapore
Description: After winning a popular TV cookery contest, lawyer-turned-chef Woo opened Ibid in a remodelled shophouse. The enthusiastic chef gets hands-on in every part of his venture from supervising the cooking and warmly greeting guests to serving the food himself. French and Italian techniques married with Asian ingredients set the scene in the different courses of the single set menu. The counter seats are the best spots to interact with the chefs and watch the alchemy unfold. Bookings advisable.

Address: Singapore Tyler Print Institute, #02-02, 41 Robertson Quay, 238236, Singapore
