Description: Since 2023, Jag has been housed in this pristine white-walled space with sage green furnishings, brushed brass trims and mid-century rattan chairs. Chef Jeremy Gillon's cooking remains vegetable-forward: French produce picked at peak ripeness – and supplemented by meats and seafood – is key to his ethos. Dishes are light in flavours but strong in creative flair. The cheese trolley impresses with its sheer variety. Round off your meal with a digestif.

Address: Esplanade Mall, #02-23, Marina Bay Promenade, 8 Raffles Avenue, 039802, Singapore
Description: Chef LG Han takes recognisable local flavours and tastes remembered from childhood as his starting point – and then reimagines and reinterprets them, using superlative ingredients from across Singapore. The result is an exciting, original and unforgettable set menu that surprises, amuses and satisfies. The restaurant’s black canvas is punctured by razor sharp lighting, while the service team are clued up and very well organised.

Address: 56 Tras Street, 078995, Singapore
Description: The name is a pun on how the cooking here revolves around the charcoal grill, brazier and tandoor. Whether you sit at the counter or in a booth, the chefs put on a performance that is visible from all the seats. On top of the ‘Discovery’ and ‘Experience’ tasting menus, there are also an à la carte and a vegetarian set menu. The food cleverly melds international flavours with South Asian techniques, courtesy of savvily-layered spices and high-end ingredients.

Address: Maxwell Food Centre, #01-56, 1 Kadayanallur Street, 069184, Singapore
Description: This clean, tidy stall is named after the three items on its menu. The rojak features pineapple, yam bean, cucumber and fried dough stick dressed in a sweet, tangy and spicy sauce. Try their made-to-order popiah, too.

Address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-28/29, 44 Holland Drive, 270044, Singapore
Description: Two adjoining stalls sell noodle soup or "dry" noodles with minced pork, pork balls or fish balls handmade on the spot. The bouncy-textured, deep-flavoured fish balls made with yellowtail are especially popular.

Address: One Fullerton, #02-02B, 1 Fullerton Road, 049213, Singapore
Description: The modern French cuisine with Asian overtones is not to be outdone by the unobstructed views of Marina Bay, smart decor and discreet service. The chef team knows the Asian F&B market inside out and the single tasting menu showcases premium seafood from all over the world, especially Japan. Natural flavours are accentuated in mindful preparations underpinned by solid skills. Closed on some public holidays, so call ahead to check.

Address: #01-01,135 Geylang Road, 389226, Singapore
Description: The owner named the restaurant after her late father and serves Cantonese and Teochew cuisines – her father's favourites. The two chefs, each with over 30 years of professional experience, excel at seafood dishes that accentuate the natural umami of seasonal produce. Some specialities have to be pre-ordered, such as the steamed and chilled fourfinger threadfin with tender flesh and generous fish oil.

Address: ABC Brickworks Market & Food Centre, #01-132, Blk 6 Jalan Bukit Merah, 150006, Singapore
Description: Its bak chor mee can be made with your choice of noodles – mee pok being the most popular. Bouncy noodles are dressed in sambal and topped with sliced pork and meatballs. Also try the noodle soup with fish balls or pork liver.

Address: Adam Food Centre, #01-09 , 2 Adam Road, 289876, Singapore
Description: Into the third generation, this family business is famous for mee soto and mee rebus, the former served in broth, the latter in a thicker gravy soup. Bold flavours are authentically Malaysian; add more coriander for extra fragrance.

Address: Duo Galleria, #01-30/31/32/33, 7 Fraser Street, 189356, Singapore
Description: An alumnus of prestigious establishments in France, the U.S. and Singapore, Chef Kevin Wong opened Seroja in 2022 to pledge his love to the Malay Archipelago. His seafood-focused tasting menus pay tribute to Malaysian culinary traditions with a generous use of local produce, spices and techniques. The plating is meticulous and artful and the flavours subtle and finely balanced. Ask about the food and wine or non-alcoholic beverage pairing.

Address: Shangri-La Hotel, Lobby Level, 22 Orange Grove Road, 258350, Singapore
Description: In a graceful dining room reminiscent of a Chinese garden, Shang Palace rolls out an extensive menu dominated by old-time Cantonese classics that are hard to find elsewhere, such as grilled chicken liver and pork fat kebabs or deep-fried pork fat medallions stuffed with crabmeat. The well-seasoned chicken boasts addictive crispy skin. Ask about the slow-boiled soups that are made with fresh ingredients and exude rich deep flavours.

Address: North Bridge Road Market & Food Centre, #01-95, 861 North Bridge Road, 198783, Singapore
Description: Get your noodle fix 24/7 at this popular stall. With myriad made-to-order options on the menu – from fish dumplings and minced pork noodles to mee tai mak and kway teow noodle soup – you're spoiled for choice.

Address: Pek Kio Market & Food Centre, #01-40, 41 Cambridge Road, 210041, Singapore
Description: It's all about rice vermicelli and egg noodles stir-fried with eggs and seafood. Homemade chili sauce enriches the flavour.

Address: Redhill Market, #01-82, 85 Redhill Lane, 150085, Singapore
Description: The braised meat platter includes pork belly, hard-boiled eggs, pork intestine, pork skin and tofu puffs – all deeply flavoured and tasty. Kway chap, or silky broad rice noodles in a soy-based soup, is served separately.

Address: Hilton Orchard, Level 35, 333 Orchard Road, 238867, Singapore
Description: Further to a recent refurbishment, the interior still exudes luxury and elegance, but in an updated, understated manner. The head chef, who honed his craft at the Tokyo branch for over 12 years, champions a refined take on Chūka Sichuan cooking. Try his signature mapo tofu, or the stir-fried Hokkaido Mangalica pork – packed with bold flavours, it is also bursting with umami, thanks to the fatty pork belly and a blend of fermented bean sauces.

Address: One Fullerton, #02-02A, 1 Fullerton Road, 049213, Singapore
Description: Hailing from Nagoya, the Japanese head chef champions a refined, elegant approach to sushi. The menus emphasise freshness and star white fish alongside other luxury seasonal produce. Ingredients are shipped from Japan four times a week and sushi rice from Yamagata and Ishikawa prefectures is mixed in a specific ratio to the best effect. Sushi is served with two sauces to accentuate the umami of the fish. The extensive sake list offers pairing options by the glass.

Address: #01-01, 17 HongKong Street, 059660, Singapore
Description: Formerly Kappo Shunsui, this atmospheric restaurant now serves three multicourse omakase menus, typically consisting of appetisers, sashimi, sushi, hot dish, main course and dessert. The interior is theatrically lit to showcase the food; the wooden counter seats 20 diners who can chat and interact with the chefs. It goes without saying that all the ingredients are top notch; the knife work is razor sharp and the sushi perfectly hand-pressed.

Address: 592 Geylang Road, 389531, Singapore
Description: The second-generation owner-chef makes every dish according to traditional recipes for guaranteed authenticity. The concise menu only features 13 items, but seasonal dishes, not on the menu, are also available. The chef’s signature dish, sweet and sour pork, is made to order, so expect to wait. The ginger chicken is simply divine – tender chicken glazed in a mild chilli sauce alongside zesty pickled ginger shoots. Also, try the kale with prawns.

Restaurant Name: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
Address: #01-01, 439 Joo Chiat Road, 427652, Singapore
Description: This simple shop has been around for over 40 years and is now run by the second generation owner. As its name suggests, bak kut teh with pepper and garlic served in a claypot is their speciality – the broth is rich, but not overpoweringly spicy and the pork ribs are tender and flavoursome. Sesame oil chicken in claypot is another highlight. The wings are succulent and the sauce delivers nutty aromas and mild sweetness. Also try local stir-fries.

Address: Blk 55, #01-59/61/63, Tiong Bahru Road, 160055, Singapore
Description: Located in a residential area, this well-known seafood restaurant has over 30 years of history to its name. They serve live seafood only, from fish to shellfish – make your selection from the tank. Don't miss the famous local choices of chilli crab and black pepper crab, which boast firm and briny sweet flesh; the local cze char dishes are also good. You can sit inside or outside – the latter area is particularly atmospheric and relaxing.

Address: 659/661 Lorong 35 Geylang, 389589, Singapore
Description: Fried rice vermicelli with crab, available for dinner, is the main event. The gigantic crab is loaded with seafood flavour; the vermicelli pick up the juices nicely, exuding scallion, ginger and chilli aromas. The other seafood dishes are also tasty.

Address: Albert Centre, #01-45, 270 Queen Street, 180270, Singapore
Description: Here, the second generation of the family sells local-style salad with pineapple, cucumber and deep-fried dough stick, tossed in a special home-made sauce and sprinkled with ground peanuts. Chilli is optional.

Address: Whampoa Makan Place, #01-32, 90/91 Whampoa Drive 91, 320091, Singapore
Description: Their famous Hokkien mee is made with rice vermicelli and yellow egg noodles, which are topped with prawns and squid for that umami flavour – even better with a helping of spicy homemade chilli sauce.

Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-44, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
Description: Serves porridge with chicken, fish or cuttlefish. Sets for one to three people are also available.

Address: 45 Amoy Street, 069871, Singapore
Description: On Amoy Street where F&B outlets abound, Solo stands out with a relaxing vibe, an action-packed open kitchen and a regularly changing Italian menu that celebrates fresh, seasonal ingredients. The 5-course gourmet menu is a great way to sample some of its signature dishes, such as al dente homemade tagliolini topped with Japanese Bafun uni bursting with briny sweetness and umami. At lunch, the 3- or 4-course seasonal set offers great value.

Address: New Bahru, #04-02, 46 Kim Yam Road, 239351, Singapore
Description: Puglian chef Mirko Febbrile creates a dining experience with a strong sense of ceremony at Somma. The lofty space in a former school library evokes grandeur right off the bat. After being greeted by the chefs at the door, diners are escorted to an open kitchen to taste some hors d'oeuvres, then seated. Every course has some kind of wow factor with a Puglian touch. The cheese course with curated drink pairings is simply ingenious.

Restaurant Name: Song Fa Bak Kut Teh (New Bridge Road)
Address: #01-01, 11 New Bridge Road, 059386, Singapore
Description: Much has changed since Mr Yeo started selling bak kut teh from his pushcart in Johor Road back in the late ’60s – nowadays it’s the second generation of the family who are running the show. They are still selling their celebrated pork ribs and peppery broth but are now doing so from 10+ shops – and this one, the simplest, seems to be the best. Queue, order, pay, and then tuck into your soup – when you’ve finished they’ll top it up for you.

Address: Clementi 448 Food Centre, #01-38, 448 Clementi Ave 3, 120448, Singapore
Description: The menu offers blanched sliced fish, deep-fried fish and fish maw, either in fish broth or bee hoon soup. Fish maw double fish soup lets you sample three items at once. Fish head, clams and shrimps are also available.

Address: Newton Food Centre, #01-37, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, 229495, Singapore
Description: The fish porridge and fish head bee hoon are the main events here. The porridge is loaded with deboned fresh mackerel that imparts deep umami and sweetness. Chinese celery and coriander instantly brighten the flavour profile.

Address: North Bridge Road Market & Food Centre, #01-105, 861 North Bridge Road, 198783, Singapore
Description: Choose between "dry" and soup noodles topped with butterflied prawns, fish cake, bean sprouts and fried garlic. The flavoursome prawn soup on the side is also a treat. Not a fan of prawns? Try the pork ribs noodles instead.

Address: IOI Central Boulevard Towers, #07-02, 2 Central Boulevard, 018916, Singapore
Description: Tucked away in an office building, Sospiri prides itself on authentic Southern Italian cooking. Handmade pasta and seafood are served in portions generous enough for sharing. Fresh ingredients such as tomatoes, wild greens and baby artichokes are deftly crafted to bring out their natural flavours. Remember to save room for its traditional tiramisu. Wine buffs will appreciate the wine list that includes a wide selection of Italian labels.

Address: Marina Bay Sands Hotel, Tower 2, Sands SkyPark, Level 57, 10 Bayfront Avenue, 018956, Singapore
Description: Wolfgang Puck’s fresh, vibrant cuisine may have been born in Beverly Hills, but its second home atop Marina Bay Sands has proven an equally good fit. The menu rolls out an enticing mix of American, Asian and European influences, with dishes ranging from honey miso broiled black cod to chicken laksa spring roll. The smoked Brisbane Valley quail seduces with addictive roasting gravy. The poolside terrace commands great views, while the elegant dining room is the epitome of cool serenity.

Address: Geylang Bahru Market & Food Centre, #01-12, 69 Geylang Bahru, 330069, Singapore
Description: This is the place to come for a comforting bowl of soup. The broth is flavourful and sweet; the spinach is crisp and fresh. You can also order stuffed tofu or seafood on top, or add mee tai mak for some starchiness.

Address: 1 Thong Soon Avenue, 787431, Singapore
Description: The birthplace of Singapore’s popular prata chain serves 20 different variations with sweet or savoury fillings. But even the basic egg prata tastes great with a crisp crust and fluffy centre - perfect for any curry in any meal.

Address: 21 Boon Tat Street, 069620, Singapore
Description: Named after the bustling train station in Colombo, this city bistro celebrates authentic Sri Lankan cuisine. The braised beef cheek with blackened coconut gravy features tender, gelatinous meat in a smoky, nutty sauce and goes well with steamed rice or roti. Ceylon arrack, the national liquor made with coconut flowers, crops up all over the menu. Try the chocolate biscuit pudding with arrack Chantilly, or their selection of artisan arrack straight.

Address: Keck Seng Tower, #B1-01, 133 Cecil Street, 069535, Singapore
Description: The owner’s family opened Singapore’s first Peranakan restaurant in 1953 – this branch has been in the CBD since 2011. Ornaments and wooden furniture lend a Chinese aesthetic. The versatile menu features dishes made with local produce and lots of spices and herbs, all prepared using traditional Chinese cooking methods. Dishes to try include ayam buah keluak (chicken with local nuts) and ikan assam nanas pedas (sweet and sour fish).

Address: Conrad Orchard, Level 3, 1 Cuscaden Road, 249715, Singapore
Description: The serene interior is furnished in contemporary Chinese style, in a palette dominated by warm whites and muted tones. On the menu, wok hei-laden stir-fries such as crocodile fillet in brown sauce, and venison with Chinese kale feature alongside Cantonese classics including baked stuffed crab shell, steamed Chinese marrow rings stuffed with shrimp, and spinach and tofu in crabmeat sauce. Be sure to try the exquisitely crafted dim sum, too.

Address: The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia, Level 3, 7 Raffles Avenue, 039799, Singapore
Description: This large, contemporary dining room is surrounded by a relaxing garden. You’ll be well looked after as the engaging staff provide service with plenty of vim and vigour. The extensive Cantonese menu covers all classics as well as seasonal dishes, with seafood being a particular highlight. The double-boiled sea whelk soup with fish maw, sauteed Dong Xing grouper fillet and braised abalone are just some of the specialities.

Address: 14 Stanley Street, 068733, Singapore
Description: In keeping with Japanese minimalist philosophy, the space is simple and serene. The bespoke 7m counter was crafted in Japan from a single piece of cypress wood. The chef has 10+ years of experience and uses Japanese fish exclusively for his sushi. To ensure freshness, seafood is flown in from Japan four times a week. In addition to the lunch and dinner omakase menus, there is the ultra-lavish Hare menu (pre-order a week ahead).

Address: #01-03, 21 Tanjong Pagar Road, 088444, Singapore
Description: Chef Katori worked at Tsukiji Market for eight years, which explains his keen eye for top-notch fish. He then moved to Singapore for a stint in a renowned sushiya, before opening his own venture in 2022. His Edomae sushi features the freshest catch from the stalls of Toyosu Market and sushi rice from Miyagi Prefecture dressed in one of two vinegar blends tailored to the type of fish. His sashimi is cut slightly thicker to accentuate the texture.

Address: South Beach Avenue, #B1-17, 26 Beach Road, 189768, Singapore
Description: This omakase sushiya with only 12 seats boasts a counter crafted from a 250-year-old hinoki tree. In stark contrast, the lively lounge for tea and dessert is clad in wallpaper with dancing cranes on a pink background. The freshest fish is creatively combined with other ingredients to great effects while the well thought-out, sometimes unorthodox, seasoning on the sushi makes the experience unique. Friendly chefs are happy to interact with diners.

Address: Shaw Centre, #01-19, 1 Scotts Road, 228208, Singapore
Description: Tokyo’s legendary sushi-ya has opened its only overseas outpost in the Lion City. Owned and supervised by chef Ryujiro Nakamura, and helmed by his young protégé, Sushi Ryujiro Singapore offers two omakase menus that include otsumami and edomae nigiri sushi. Japanese rice is dressed in a blend of four red vinegars; most ingredients are also shipped from Japan for authenticity. With only 14 counter seats, reservations are essential.

Address: The Capitol Kempinski Hotel, #01-88, 15 Stamford Road, 178906, Singapore
Description: The space is simple yet elegant, befitting the hotel that houses it. There is a 10-seat counter made from a 200-year-old cypress tree from Nara, Japan, plus a private room. Chef-owner Sakuta works closely with the all-Japanese kitchen team, creating a season-driven omakase menu based exclusively on Japanese fish. Even the rice is a blend of two Japanese cultivars in a precise ratio for the perfect texture. Every item is prepared with utmost care.

Address: 6B Dempsey Road, 247662, Singapore
Description: The duo of chefs chose to open this sushi-ya in serene surroundings away from the busy CBD. In the same vein, the wood-rich interior is minimal and Zen-inspired. All the ingredients are shipped from Japan four times a week for peak freshness. Three seasonal menus are available and attention to detail is visible at every level – Yamagata rice is dressed in a blend of three red vinegars for the perfect tartness that complements oily fish.

Address: Taman Jurong Market & Food Centre, #03-145, 3 Yung Sheng Road, Jurong West, 618499, Singapore
Description: This third-generation family business prides itself on its flavoursome fish soup made from scratch and served with sliced fish, deep-fried fish or fish head. Order noodles, rice or congee on the side for a complete meal.

Address: Hong Lim Market and Food Centre, #02-16, Blk 531A, Upper Cross Street, 051531, Singapore
Description: Noodles served with soup meat balls, dried fish and pork liver.

Address: Paragon, #B1-44, 290 Orchard Road, 238859, Singapore
Description: Since 1981, the Indonesian chefs at Tambuah Mas have been making authentic home-style dishes from Padang, Sulawesi and Java. Family recipes with delicate blends of spices and precise preparations are closely guarded secrets, passed down over generations. The signature tahu telor (deep-fried egg-coated tofu cubes in a dark sweet sauce) boasts crispy skin and perfect briny-sweetness. Always round off a meal here with a cendol.

Address: Chinatown Complex Market & Food Centre, #02-048, 335 Smith Street, 050335, Singapore
Description: Come here for the quintessential Singaporean teatime classics – kaya toast with kopi kosong (black coffee). This popular stall opened its doors in the 1950s and locals have been lining up to get their caffeine fix ever since.

Address: 97 Tanjong Pagar Road, 088518, Singapore
Description: This is one of the most popular little gems in Chinatown and it’s easy to see why. The narrow house offers dining on three floors; art by local artists add colour and character. In business for over 20 years, regulars keep returning for its aromatic cooking like Ngo Heong that delivers all the subtle and authentic flavours of Peranakan, as well as addictive sweets like Chendol. Better still, prices are as generous as the portions—that are great for sharing.

Address: 269 Beach Road, 199546, Singapore
Description: This whitewashed traditional shophouse evokes unmistakably tropical vibes – wicker back chairs, wallpaper with banana leaf prints and cheerful blue-and-white tiled flooring. On the menu, the coconut theme is also obvious – the nasi lemak set is the best seller, but other dishes deserve equal attention too, such as ayam goreng berempah (spiced fried chicken with crispy rempah crumbs), and sago pudding with pandan, palm sugar and coconut cream.

Address: 48 Peck Seah Street, 079317, Singapore
Description: Earthy shades, Moorish motifs and rattan pendant lights exude Middle Eastern warmth. The room sports two dining vibes: a friendly bar at the front or views of the open kitchen to the rear. The chefs put a contemporary spin on Arabic cuisine from hummus, kebab and falafel to whole roast chicken and grilled seabass. Alternatively, order ‘Feed Me’ and let the chefs decide. Come with a posse to share the food and the fun.

Address: 16 Mohamed Sultan Road, 238965, Singapore
Description: Chef Mano Thevar serves a creative multi-course menu rooted in Indian traditions and crafted with European techniques. Signature dishes such as Chettinad chicken roti or Brittany lobster in curry beurre blanc pack a ton of oomph, while maintaining a fine balance with mindful touches. A vegetarian version is available but needs pre-ordering. The wine list covers 600+ labels; ask about wine, sake and non-alcoholic drink pairings.

Address: Maxwell Food Centre, #01-10/11, 1 Kadayanallur Street, 069184, Singapore
Description: Expect a long queue, but the velvety chicken with springy skin is worth the wait. Even the aromatic oil rice and briny-sweet sauce are perfectly made. Consider ordering half a chicken to share, or an extra drumstick.

Address: Taman Jurong Market & Food Centre, #02-66, 3 Yung Sheng Road, Jurong West, 618499, Singapore
Description: Open mornings only, this stall is famous for its Cantonese barbecue that tends to sell out quickly - so come early! Roast duck boasts velvety meat without being too fatty and the roast pork strikes a fine balance between lean and fatty meat.

Restaurant Name: Tiong Bahru Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
Address: Tiong Bahru Market, #02-82, 30 Seng Poh Road, 168898, Singapore
Description: The rice that comes with the signature Hainanese boneless chicken imparts a mild turmeric aroma. Tender juicy meat, without too much fat under the bouncy, gelatinous skin. The roast chicken is also recommended.

Restaurant Name: Tiong Bahru Lien Fa Shui Jing Pau
Address: Alexandra Village Food Centre, #01-10, Blk 120 Bukit Merah Lane 1, 150120, Singapore
Description: The teochew dumplings are stuffed with jicama for a lovely crunch, while chopped dried shrimps lend briny umami. Try them with the home-made chilli sauce. Dumplings with red bean or taro paste filling are available after 1pm.

Address: 51 Old Airport Road Food Centre, #01-135/136, 51 Old Airport Road, 390051, Singapore
Description: This kway chap stall serves the broad rice noodles with pork belly, trotters, intestine, tripe and dried tofu braised in a spiced soy-based marinade. Noodles are thin and silky; braised pork and tofu impart deep flavours and aromas.

Address: Geylang Bahru Market & Food Centre, #01-68, 69 Geylang Bahru, 330069, Singapore
Description: The stall carries three kinds of handmade dumplings – soon kueh stuffed with jicama, rice kueh and kuchai kueh with chives. All varieties boast elastic skin and generous filling.

Address: #01-02, 26 Dempsey Road, 249686, Singapore
Description: A nod to the heyday of Italian cinema, the interior takes you back to the Adriatic Riviera circa 1960s. The red-yellow-blue colour scheme is carried through from the walls to the tableware. The concept by celebrity chef Massimo Bottura involves whimsically and creatively harnessing Italian produce in signature dishes like artisan tortellini in a silky sauce made with parmigiano reggiano aged for 36 months. Stone-baked pizzas are delicious.

Restaurant Name: Tow Kwar Pop Tiong Bahru Market
Address: Tiong Bahru Market, #02-06, 30 Seng Poh Road, 168898, Singapore
Description: Here, the rojak is made with sliced cucumber, apple and bean sprouts, topped with either crispy tofu puffs or fried dough sticks. The syrupy dressing is rich and tangy, and the ground peanuts give the salad a lovely crunch.

Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-12, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
Description: Hakkanese Lui Cha is a soupy rice dish in which chicken, cabbage and pickles meet the nuttiness of sesame and peanuts plus a hint of herbs. Order the fish cake, stuffed tofu or fried egg toppings.

Address: 47/49 Armenian Street, 179937, Singapore
Description: It’s less like walking into a restaurant, more like falling into the warm embrace of a much loved family member. Here it’s about nostalgia and paying homage to the food, history and customs of the Peranakans – you’ll find all the classic dishes, prepared in an authentic way, and the hard part is narrowing down your choice. The setting really is unique and the Ayam Buah Keluak is one of the signature.

Address: Hotel Michael, #02-142/143, Resorts World Sentosa, 26 Sentosa Gateway, 098138, Singapore
Description: Clever lighting, dark wood and shades of red lend this modern Chinese restaurant a slick, stylish feel. Amidst traditional recipes, novel dishes also feature on the menu. Either way, the food is always meticulously plated. Don’t miss the fish bone and fish maw soup, double-boiled with chicken and pork for six hours. Chilli crab served in a casserole boasts firm, flavoursome meat. Order deep-fried buns to mop up the knockout sauce.

Address: #01-02, 57 South Bridge Road, 058688, Singapore
Description: Though its name means ‘anything goes’, this restaurant is exceptionally specific about the food it serves – Isan cuisine hailing from north-eastern Thailand and famous for its infernal heat. The PenLaos signature chicken is marinated with white peppercorns and coriander for three days before being grilled to perfection. Leng zaab is pork ribs in a spicy sour broth that is simply addictive. Ask for the house-made Isan tamarind dip to dunk the pork in.

Address: 115 Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre, #01-30, Blk 115 Bukit Merah View, 151115, Singapore
Description: Not to be confused with the western sweet of the same name, carrot cake here is savoury, made with radish and stir-fried in seasoning. Opt for the dark version coated in egg, and tossed in sticky, caramelised dark soy sauce.

Address: #01-01, 57 Tras Street, 078996, Singapore
Description: This chef puts a new spin on classic kaiseki with two Wagyu set menus that honour a head-to-tail concept. He chooses Ozaki beef from Miyazaki, otherwise unavailable in Singapore, for its gutsy flavour. Various cuts from 32- to 36-month-old cattle are prepared in a myriad of ways to highlight their textures and umami. Most of the other ingredients are flown in from Japan to ensure authenticity. There is also an á la carte menu for add-on courses.

Address: OUE Bayfront, Level 19, 50 Collyer Quay, 049321, Singapore
Description: Aptly named after the French word for ‘view’, this romantic restaurant boasts one of the most stunning vistas of Marina Bay. Even the ceiling is designed to emanate light without casting reflections on the glass panes. The menu shows the culinary vision of the young head chef, with the four-course chef’s tasting menu being the most popular choice where diners may choose from a number of interesting options. Steaks and risotto are great for sharing. Executive set lunch is popular.

Address: Carlton Hotel, Level 2, 76 Bras Basah Road, 189558, Singapore
Description: A loyal clientele has made this comfortable, classically decorated Cantonese restaurant their own. The chef was born in Guangzhou but really developed his culinary skills and honed his craft in Hong Kong. His Cantonese dishes range from banquet delicacies like abalone and bird’s nest soup to seafood dishes such as steamed fish. There are also Cantonese roast meats, claypot dishes and home-style items like steamed minced pork with salted fish.

Address: The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands, Level 2 Dining, L2-03, 10 Bayfront Avenue, 018956, Singapore
Description: The contemporary room is divided into three sections: a counter with seats, private rooms and the chef’s table. To stay close to the action, opt for the latter. Dinner features one sitting only with a choice between traditional and seasonal menus. Ingredients are of high quality and the food is nicely crafted. In addition to typical Japanese fare, some dishes are underscored by Western techniques with a pronounced Italian accent at times.

Address: Marina Bay Sands Hotel, Tower 2, Lobby, 10 Bayfront Avenue, 018972, Singapore
Description: This more accessible spinoff of its upscale sister Waku Ghin is the brainchild of the eponymous chef Tetsuya Wakuda. All rooms feature the traditional Japanese craft of wood joinery prominently, alongside soft lighting, tan leather chairs and banquettes. The menu offers an array of modern Japanese classics made with quality ingredients sourced globally. Adding original cocktails and a buzzy vibe to the equation, Wakuda guarantees a fun night out.

Restaurant Name: Whampoa Soya Bean & Grass Jelly Drinks
Address: Whampoa Makan Place, #01-52, 90/91 Whampoa Drive 91, 320091, Singapore
Description: Tofu pudding is freshly made on the spot – just add toppings such as grass jelly, red beans or lotus seeds. Or try their drinkable versions, in which the soybean flavour is complemented by the velvety texture of a smoothie.

Address: Chijmes, #01-26/27, 30 Victoria Street, 187996, Singapore
Description: Chef Takuya Yamashita’s style is to use French techniques to bring out the best of the mostly Japanese ingredients. The resulting tasting menus are inventive and intriguing and feature delicate and attractive dishes, such as Hokkaido scallop with Mont D’Or, and Miyazaki Wagyu with cognac sauce. The graceful restaurant is housed within a historic converted convent and is divided into two rooms, one of which allows diners to see into the kitchen.

Address: 76 Peck Seah Street, 079331, Singapore
Description: ‘Vegetarian cuisine for non-vegetarians’ is how the team describes their longstanding Thai and Peranakan restaurant. Meat-like textures and flavours are achieved by clever preparations of soy product and tofu. The tangy, crispy mango tamarind tofu roll is jazzed up with Penang rendang, herbs and spices, while the mushrooms deliver a texture that is almost indistinguishable from meat. The cosy interior is simple and bright. Portions big enough to share.

Address: 39 HongKong Street, 059678, Singapore
Description: After working in some prestigious kitchens, Chef Nicolas Tam makes his debut with this intimate, understated and well-run restaurant. His solid French techniques come through in his pan-Asian tasting menu featuring mostly Japanese ingredients, sporting refinement, precision and balance. Served and introduced by the chefs themselves, the courses flow seamlessly and build upon each other. Counter seats overlooking the kitchen are the ones to go for.

Address: Redhill Market, #01-94, 85 Redhill Lane, 150085, Singapore
Description: For over 30 years, locals have been coming here for the fried hor fun (flat rice noodles) – laden with wok hei, nicely charred and in a sauce that clings to the noodles. Choose from beef, fish or assorted toppings, and don't miss the cracklings.

Restaurant Name: Xing Yun Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
Address: Yuhua Market & Hawker Centre, #01-202, Blk 347, Jurong East Avenue 1, Jurong East, 600347, Singapore
Description: Its signature Hainanese boneless chicken rice is garnished with pineapple, tomato and cucumber. Dip the juicy, silky chicken in the briny-sweet chilli and ginger sauce before savouring it with the aromatic rice.

Address: The St. Regis Hotel, Level 1U, 29 Tanglin Road, 247911, Singapore
Description: Since the name translates as ‘Banquet Court’, it's no surprise to find a very comfortable space, ideal for impressing visitors and friends. The head chef has extensive experience when it comes to traditional dishes, especially Cantonese barbecue and double-boiled soups. Try his crispy roast pork belly for the ultimate indulgence. He's also an expert at preparing live fish – choose from 11 cooking styles. At lunch, don't miss his Hong Kong-style dim sum.

Address: Beauty World Food Centre #04-26, 144 Upper Bukit Timah Road, 588177, Singapore
Description: The owner learned to make cendol in Malacca, and his rice flour jelly worms – made on the spot – are softer than most. On top of the classic cendol shaved ice, add red kidney beans, palm seeds, corn kernels or durian.

Address: #01-04, 36 Purvis Street, 188613, Singapore
Description: Founded in the 1990s by a couple with a passion for Thai cuisine, this restaurant is spread over three colourful Thai-style rooms. Added authenticity comes courtesy of the helpful waitresses in traditional dress. The Thai and Thai-Chinese dishes are prepared with fresh ingredients sourced daily. Start your meal with som tom: papaya salad with dried shrimps and peanuts. Consider ordering the set if you find the lengthy à la carte menu hard to navigate.

Address: Raffles Arcade, #03-02, 328 North Bridge Road, 188719, Singapore
Description: The chef honed his remarkable skills while working in China for many years. He returned to Singapore and opened Yi – the Chinese word for art and craftsmanship, hence the fancy dining room adorned in exquisite paper art and the food that reflects eclectic influences from all over China. Steamed free range chicken in herbal broth impresses by its umami and mild herbal aftertaste. Also check out the seasonal menu bursting with creative twists.

Restaurant Name: Yi Pin Wei Braised Duck Kway Chap
Address: Tampines Round Market & Food Centre, #01-40, 137 Tampines Street 11, 521137, Singapore
Description: In addition to their signature braised duck, they also serve pork trotter and chitterlings. The kway chap set menu enables you to sample different cuts all at once in a mild herbal broth. The stall also features rice dishes and kway teow.

Address: 115 Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre, #01-56, Blk 115 Bukit Merah View, 151115, Singapore
Description: The owner has his springy eggy noodles tailor-made. They are best enjoyed in its “dry” form – blanched and dressed in a savoury sweet sauce. Wonton with minced pork is fresh and firm.

Address: Suntec City Mall, Tower 5, #01-444, 3 Temasek Boulevard, 038983, Singapore
Description: The first overseas outpost of the Shanghainese F&B brand opened in Singapore in 2024. The menu predominantly features quality live seafood from Zhejiang, prepared in authentic Ningbo style. ‘Ningbo 18 cuts’ is raw crab marinated in spiced soy; each piece brims with orange roe that tastes gooey and buttery. Save room for Ningbo sticky rice balls filled with runny black sesame paste that are made to order. Tastefully appointed interior.

Restaurant Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Address: Taman Jurong Market & Food Centre, #02-78, 3 Yung Sheng Road, Jurong West, 618499, Singapore
Description: Pork rib soup is served in a claypot alongside other condiments, such as peppercorns. The Chinese herbal version strikes a fine balance, with distinctive yet not overpowering herbal flavours. Other claypot soups are also available.

Address: People's Park Complex Food Centre, #01-1084, 32 New Market Road, 050032, Singapore
Description: There is only one thing on the menu – assorted tofu stew. Fish balls, tofu skin rolls, silken tofu and deep-fried tofu stuffed with minced fish are ladled into your bowl alongside a clear broth seasoned by scallion. Simply delicious.

Address: Tampines Round Market & Food Centre, #01-45, 137 Tampines Street 11, 521137, Singapore
Description: The signature kolo mee set menu is a tour de force starring everything the stall has to offer – braised spareribs, wontons, char siew and curly, bouncy kolo noodles dressed in lard and shallot oil. Ipoh hor fun is also available.

Address: #01-205, 253 Jurong East Steet 24, 600253, Singapore
Description: The fish head curry boasts velvety flesh loaded with umami and is hot and spicy, perfect with steamed rice. Besides its eponymous dish, other equally stunning fish dishes and stir-fries are also available.

Address: 41 Bukit Pasoh Road, 089855, Singapore
Description: The celebrity chef of Frantzén fame has opened his third Asian venture in this shophouse. Diners are offered an aperitif and amuse-bouche on the first floor, before the eight-course neo-Nordic, seafood-slanted tasting menu with Japanese influences unfolds on the second floor. The onion course is a tour de force whose flavours are intensified by contrasting textures and temperatures. The non-alcoholic drink pairing sees eccentric combos that nonetheless work.

Restaurant Name: Zhang Ji Shanghai La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Address: Alexandra Village Food Centre, #01-56, Blk 120 Bukit Merah Lane 1, 150120, Singapore
Description: Besides xiao long bao, this busy stall offers an array of Shanghainese food, such as pan fried dumplings, sour and spicy soup. Their pork and chives potstickers are filled to the brim and nicely browned on the bottom.

Restaurant Name: Zheng Zhi Wen Ji Pig Organ Soup
Address: Clementi 448 Food Centre, #01-26, 448 Clementi Ave 3, 120448, Singapore
Description: As well as pork offal, the menu features marinated pork trotter, kway chap and bak kut teh. But the noodle soup with pork liver and kidney stands out – the offal is cooked perfectly and the broth loaded with herbal aromas.

Restaurant Name: Zhi Wei Xian Zion Road Big Prawn Noodle
Address: Zion Riverside Food Centre, #04, 70 Zion Road, 247792, Singapore
Description: The soup has a rich prawn flavour. Fresh prawns, chili and pork rinds combine to make a great bowl of noodles.

Address: #01-01, 458 MacPherson Road, 368176, Singapore
Description: Formerly One Prawn & Co, Zhup Zhup still sees constant queues forming beneath its red awning. Book ahead to cut your wait time. The signature prawn noodles come in a set: a bowl of noodles plus rich prawn soup in a claypot. Out of the four types of noodles, the classic option is yellow noodles with thin bee hoon. The soup is loaded with flavours, imparted in particular by the tomalley of countless prawn heads.

Restaurant Name: Zi Jing Cheng Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
Address: Alexandra Village Food Centre, #01-15, Blk 120 Bukit Merah Lane 1, 150120, Singapore
Description: There is only one thing on the menu – Hainanese boneless chicken rice. Set menus are available for one to three guests, all served with steamed chicken, rice and soup. The bird is tender and flavoursome. Expect to queue any time.
